item.title: Spontaneous Ferroelectric Nematic Ordering from an Isotropic Liquid in All-Atom Molecular Dynamics Simulations
item.description: Ferroelectric nematic (NF) liquid crystals are fluids with macroscopic polar order, yet the molecular pathway by which an isotropic liquid spontaneously develops long-range polar order remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that microsecond-scale, unbiased all-atom molecular dynamics simulations can reproduce the spontaneous development of strong, system-wide polar order from an isotropic state. For DIO, highly polar local domains emerged upon cooling but remained nanoscopic because slow molecular diffusion might suppress their further growth. In contrast, UUZU-2-N, which exhibits an enantiotropic NF phase at relatively high temperatures, developed progressively stronger global polar order, ultimately reaching a nearly monodomain state with a polar order parameter of . The calculated spontaneous polarization reached 6.7 μC/cm2, in reasonable agreement with experiment. Nematic orientational order developed rapidly, whereas long-range polar order continued to develop over several microseconds. The spontaneous development of strong polar order was also reproduced for C2-BOE. Structural analyses revealed characteristic offset configurations and head-to-tail correlations between neighboring molecules. Comparison with molecular electrostatic distributions suggests that longitudinally asymmetric and modulated charge distributions contribute to stabilizing these polar arrangements. These results provide atomistic insights into the development of collective polar order and its associated local packing in the NF liquid crystals.

item.title: Where machine learning for enantioselectivity on polysaccharide chiral stationary phases actually fails: a leave-one-paper-out reappraisal of 10,525 enantiomer pairs
item.description: Machine-learning models for enantioselectivity on polysaccharide chiral stationary phases increasingly report high accuracy, but almost always under random data splits. We re-examined this problem on CMRT, the largest public chiral chromatography dataset, curating it into 10,525 enantiomer pairs covering 530 DOI groupsand25columns.Underatrueleave-one-paper-outprotocol,elution-orderaccuracyfallsfrom 66.1 % under a random split to 52.9 %, indistinguishable from a within-paper permutation null (52.3 % ± 0.6). Between-paper variance accounts for 38.5 % of the total variance, but it cannot be predicted from compositional features, so domain adaptation is ineffective. The molecular signal is real within a single paper (median per-paper correlation r = +0.185) but falls to r = +0.0009 for an unseen paper, and adding trainingpapersdoesnothelp.Avariancedecompositionofasingle-laboratorygridshowsthatonly 23.05 % of the variance is attributable to additive main effects of molecule and condition, the remaining 76.95 % being an unidentifiable molecule × condition interaction and noise. We therefore argue that the bottleneck liesnotinmodelcapacityordescriptorqualitybutinthedatastructure:adding condition metadata,buildingsystematicmolecule×conditiongrids,introducingreplicatemeasurementsand recording failed separations are the prerequisites for improving transferability.

item.title: Matrix-dependent transformation governs the chemical identity and biological fate of a metal–organic framework
item.description: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are generally described by their pristine structures, although aqueous use and release expose them to ligands and dissolved ions that can reconstruct their coordination chemistry before biological contact. Here, we follow HKUST-1 across an environmental-to-biological exposure cascade using complementary X-ray methods. Time-resolved Cu K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) showed rapid, matrix-specific disruption of the Cu-carboxylate paddlewheel in borehole water (BHW) and serum-free cell-culture medium (CCM). In XANES linear-combination fitting (LCF), the spectral fraction represented by pristine HKUST-1 became unresolved in BHW by 24 h and decreased to 4.1% in CCM by 4 h. The transformed solids were represented predominantly by carbonate-/hydroxide-like Cu environments in BHW and phosphate-, CuCl-, and CuO-reference-like environments in CCM. Powder X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, Cu Kβ valence-to-core X-ray emission spectroscopy, carbon K-edge X-ray Raman scattering, and electron microscopy showed that transformation extended from the Cu ligand field to BTC carboxylate coordination, medium- and long-range order, and morphology. CCM generated operational <0.02 µm Cu at an initial rate of µg mL-1 h-1, compared with µg mL-1 h-1 in BHW, yet low sustained Cu mobilization in BHW did not indicate persistence of the parent framework. On a nominal material-mass basis, BHW aging increased apparent acute potency toward Daphnia magna, lowering the 48 h EC50 from 0.54 to 0.18 µg mL-1. Cryogenic X-ray fluorescence mapping and spatially resolved XANES showed further Cu re-coordination during gastrointestinal transit. Following pristine-material exposure, the HKUST-1-like contribution decreased from 10.7% in the foregut to 0.2% in the hindgut, whereas 86–98% of the Cu signal following BHW-aged-material exposure was represented by non-HKUST-1 environments throughout the gut. Framework disruption is therefore followed by matrix-selected reconstruction and biological ligand exchange. MOF performance and environmental health depend on the exposure-conditioned material, not on pristine structure or dissolved-metal concentration alone.

item.title: Schema-guided zero-shot decision models for chemical synthesis argument roles: comparison with supervised ChemBERT
item.description: Jev and Clef outperform a released ChemBERT classifier supervised on the Organic Synthesis Procedures with Argument Roles (OSPAR) corpus on a human-adjudicated Creative Commons (CC) synthesis reference. With supplied mention spans, 17 procedures provide 288 resolved operation–candidate pairs: the positive-role micro-averaged F1 score (the precision–recall harmonic mean) is 96.59% for Jev, 95.27% for Clef and 90.36% for ChemBERT. Fixed role definitions are used without prompt demonstrations or author-performed task-specific fine-tuning; prior OSPAR-based prompt development is disclosed. A new retrospective evaluation applies the same configurations and scoring to 258 pairs from 11 OSPAR test procedures, yielding 97.92, 94.64 and 97.38%, respectively. Clef’s point-estimate ordering relative to ChemBERT therefore changes between corpora. These OSPAR procedures were previously viewed during development, so the extension supplies a matched source-corpus comparison rather than untouched validation. A fresh CC repeat is reported separately. Reference-convention and sentence-boundary sensitivities clarify the scope of the CC advantage. Clef-flash reaches 78.96% in the original CC evaluation, with negative-pair rejection limiting precision. Separately, ChemBERT’s CC exact-span and joint-relation F1 are 84.42 and 74.61%. The study demonstrates strong role assignment without additional task training while separating corpus dependence, rejection and mention recovery from complete synthesis extraction.

item.title: From Physiological Variations to Institutional Barriers: A Qualitative Inquiry into the Academic and Professional Life Cycles of Color-Vision Deficient Chemistry Students
item.description: Promoting diversity and inclusion for students with diverse visual abilities is crucial for advancing equity in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education. While existing research heavily focuses on macro-level laboratory modifications and instructional accommodations, the systemic and psychological barriers faced by chemistry researchers with mild color-vision deficiency (CVD) remain largely underexplored. Guided by the Social Model of Disability, this study critically distinguishes between biological "impairment" and sociostructurally "disability" to investigate how a century-old, rigid screening tool—Ishihara's pseudoisochromatic plates—forces functional individuals into a cycle of marginalization and academic anxiety. Using a constructivist qualitative approach, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 CVD undergraduate and graduate chemistry students, alongside two medical professionals and three university administrators across five institutions. The thematic analysis reveals that standardized "one-size-fits-all" screening practices inflict severe institutional trauma and erode students' academic self-efficacy, triggering persistent self-doubt despite their actual functional equivalence in modern laboratories. Facing anachronistic policy regulations and extensive workplace stigmatization, participants often resort to "compulsory masking" or concealment strategies to navigate graduate admissions and career entry, occasionally resorting to legal resistance such as labor arbitration. Furthermore, collaborative learning environments exhibit an aesthetic hegemony where peers' resistance to adaptive, high-contrast designs translates into verbal microaggressions.

item.title: LANaPDB: A web-based platform for the Latin American Natural Product Database
item.description: Natural products (NPs) have a major impact on several research areas, including drug discovery and development, food and agricultural chemistry, and the cosmetic industry. Annotated compound databases of NPs provide a structured and organized framework that facilitates access to information, particularly if the compound database is freely available. Over the past few years, a compound library from eight countries, called the Latin American Natural Product Database (LANaPDB), has been assembled, curated, and annotated and currently contains 14,741 unique compounds. The compounds are annotated with extensive bioactivity data retrieved from the peer-reviewed literature, along with structural information (e.g., chirality, taxonomic and structural classification), accessibility (commercial availability or estimated synthetic feasibility), and other properties of interest in drug discovery. Although all the information in LANaPDB is in the public domain and documented in the peer-reviewed literature, it was not available through a free website that enabled rapid and intuitive access to all the information. The goal of this manuscript is to introduce and describe a freely available web server dedicated to systematically and intuitively exploring the contents of LANaPDB. The website provides a dynamic interface that spans from basic to advanced structural and information search, multi-parameter filtering, interactive visualization of phylogenetic and chemotaxonomic diversity, geographical mapping of compound origins, and molecular structure rendering. It is also possible to download the entire compound database from the website. The website facilitates the exploration of Latin American NPs and multidisciplinary research. The web-based platform of LANaPDB is https://www.lanapdb.com/.

item.title: Excited-state dynamics and photo-reaction pathways of 4-nitrothiophenol in solution investigated by time-resolved soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy
item.description: Understanding the molecular pathways underlying light-driven reactions is essential for developing efficient and sustainable photochemical processes. Here, we investigate the photoinduced dynamics and reactivity of deprotonated 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) in aqueous solution using transient nitrogen and oxygen K-edge near-edge X-ray absorption fine structure (NEXAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) and equation-of-motion coupled-cluster (EOM-CC) calculations. Valence-state calculations identify the lowest bright excited state S1 as a ππ∗ state with partial charge-transfer character, consistent with the experimentally observed absorption maximum near 408 nm. Following excitation at 343 nm, transient NEXAFS reveals the formation and reaction pathways of both singlet and triplet excited states. The combined experimental and theoretical results indicate that intersystem crossing proceeds from the vibrationally hot S1 state through the higher-lying T2 state, followed by rapid internal conversion to T1. The S1 state additionally undergoes photodissociation on the nanosecond timescale, producing NO2 and a thiophenyl radical. In parallel, the T1 state reacts with dissolved O2, leading to formation of the 4-NTP radical and reactive oxygen species, including hydroxyl radicals. oxygen K-edge measurements provide direct evidence for the formation and persistence of these oxygen-centered reactive intermediates. These results establish distinct singlet-and triplet-mediated reaction channels in aqueous 4-NTP and demonstrate the capability of elementspecific transient X-ray spectroscopy, supported by high-level EOM-CC calculations, to resolve competing excited-state pathways and photochemical reactions in solution.

item.title: Aggregation-Driven Self-Inhibition of Grignard Reagents: Insights from DFT and Microkinetic Modeling
item.description: A mechanistic DFT study with explicit Et2O microsolvation and microkinetic modeling unveils how organomagnesium reagents (nBuMgX, X = Cl, Br, nBu) undergo structural reorganization during nitrile additions, generating aggregates that hamper reactivity. Starting from halide-bridged dimers (Et2O)·nBuMg(µ-X)2MgnBu·(Et2O), nitrile addition proceeds via a bimetallic 6-centered transition state (∆G‡ ∼ 19 kcal mol−1) and yields imido-bridged products stabilized by more than 30 kcal mol−1. For mixed reagents (X = Cl, Br), post-nucleophilic addition Schlenk equilibria lead to di-imido dimers (Et2O)·XMg(µ-[N])2MgX·(Et2O) along with the initial reactive dimer. In contrast, starting from the homoleptic nBu2Mg, post-nucleophilic addition equilibria deliver a Mg-based tetramer Mg4(µ-[N])4nBu4 that scavenges nucleophilic groups. Engaging the remaining Mg–alkyl bonds in such a tetramer requires overcoming an overall energy barrier of 27 kcal mol−1, thus limiting conversion. Microkinetic simulations, based on computed free energy profiles and experimental initial conditions, quantitatively reproduce the experimental 50% conversion plateau and 4:1 product:side product ratio, establishing aggregation-driven inhibition as the origin of incomplete reactivity. These findings provide rational guidelines for optimizing Grignard transformations through reagent selection, additive strategies and solvation engineering, with applications for polyolefin upgrading and pharmaceutical synthesis.

item.title: Drying, ageing and reducibility of Ru catalysts obtained via deposition-precipitation: the hidden role of water
item.description: Ruthenium catalysts prepared by deposition–precipitation (DP) contain highly hydrated oxidized Ru species whose structure and evolution remain difficult to define. Here, Ru catalysts supported on alumina and two activated carbons were investigated to clarify how support chemistry and water content affect the Ru phase formed by DP. HR-TEM, O K-edge NEXAFS, H2-TPR and CO chemisorption reveal marked support-dependent differences in Ru aggregation, local oxygen coordination, reducibility and site accessibility. On alumina, hydrated Ru oxy-hydroxide species coexist with RuO2-like local domains, whereas carbon supports stabilize predominantly hydroxylated and structurally disordered Ru environments. Post-synthesis drying and ageing progressively alter these properties through dehydration, with markedly different consequences depending on the support. On alumina, water removal promotes structural consolidation and RuO2-like ordering, making the Ru(IV) → Ru(III) → Ru(0) reduction sequence kinetically resolvable while decreasing the population of accessible Ru sites. On activated carbons, dehydration mainly affects site accessibility without inducing comparable RuO2-like ordering. Catalytic transfer hydrogenolysis of diphenyl ether (DPE) provides a first catalytic assessment of these differences: DPE conversion follows the same trend as CO-accessible Ru sites, while aromatic yield does not increase proportionally with activity because consecutive hydrogenation is also promoted. These results identify water as a transient structural component of DP-derived Ru catalysts and show that drying and storage history are integral to controlling their reducibility, site accessibility and catalytic behavior.

item.title: X-Ray Diffraction Model for Spiral-Growth-Driven Defects in Layered Thin Films
item.description: Out-of-phase boundary (OPB) defects are a hallmark of spiral-driven growth in Aurivillius phase thin films, often arising from screw dislocation-mediated layer propagation. These boundaries are associated with localised strain gradients and modify polarisation and diffraction responses. Existing analytical XRD models that treat OPBs as planar or parallel features have limitations in capturing the vertical gradient in lattice displacement and the angular asymmetry observed in spiral-grown films. In this work, we introduce a generalised model that represents OPBs as stacked pyramidal defects along the film thickness, as observed in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) cross sections. The model incorporates a three dimensional structure factor formalism that accounts for atomic positions, fractional lattice displacements, the inclination of the OPB boundaries and other parameters. Simulated X-ray diffraction patterns based on this model reproduce the asymmetric peak broadening and splitting observed in Bi4Ti3O12 thin films with high fidelity and enable a non-destructive estimation of OPB density, and a more realistic description of defect geometry than planar models allow. This work establishes a three-dimensional, predictive framework for spiralmediated OPB defects in layered ferroelectric oxides, offering a basis for defect engineering and materials optimisation in future memory and neuromorphic applications.

item.title: Structure–Processing–Architecture–Property Relationships and Scalability in Renewable Polymer Selection for Sustainable Biomaterials
item.description: Renewable biopolymers are increasingly explored as alternatives to fossil-derived materials, yet bio-based origin alone does not determine performance or commercial relevance. This review compares alginate, lignin, cellulose, chitosan, and starch through an integrated structure–processing–architecture–property–scalability framework. Molecular functionality is linked to processing pathways and to the resulting coatings, fibers, crosslinked networks, porous structures, carbon materials, and composite architectures. A dedicated cross-cutting discussion then argues why three comparison axes common in the existing literature, chemistry, biodegradability, and application category, each fail, on their own, to predict which material and processing combination is actually useful for a given job, and what a comparison needs to include instead. The review closes with application-specific design rules to support material and processing selection for sustainable packaging, thermal management, water purification and separations, carbon capture, energy storage and electrocatalysis, biomedical scaffolds and controlled release, and construction materials.

item.title: Publication-block calibration reveals wide uncertainty in PLGA release endpoint prediction
item.description: Literature-mined release curves can support model development while overstating applicability to an unseen publication. We test the consequences of changing the uncertainty unit from a release observation to a formulation and then an entire publication block. A unit-audited public PLGA dataset provides 1-, 3-, and 7day endpoints for 257 formulations from 99 DOI groups. Fixed single-threaded baselines are evaluated with five prespecified 60/20/20 publication train/calibration/test partitions. The primary outcome is simultaneous coverage of every eligible formulation endpoint within a held-out publication. Extra-trees MAE was 0.172 release fraction under publication splitting, versus 0.136 under formulation-random splitting; mean publication-split R2 was 0.002. Pooled-point calibration yielded 68% empirical publication coverage, compared with 88% for publication-max calibration. Mean widths were 0.583 and 0.773, respectively, on a physical 0-1 scale. Additional capacity, feature-block and learning-curve ablations use the same publication holdouts. Only 1.6% of harmonized endpoints coincide with a recorded source time, motivating a resolution audit. Publicationlevel calibration improves empirical simultaneous coverage at the cost of wide intervals; exchangeability and prospective performance remain unestablished.

item.title: Computational Modeling of Electrolytes and the Solid–Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) in Li-Ion Batteries: A 30-Year Odyssey from DFT/MD/MC to AI–A Comprehensive Review
item.description: The solid electrolyte interphase (SEI)—the passivating nanometric film that forms on anode surfaces in lithium-ion batteries—remains one of the most critical yet least understood components in electrochemical energy storage. Unraveling its formation, structure, and evolution has proven to be a formidable odyssey, spanning decades of relentless effort and confronting researchers with challenges as daunting as those faced by the ancient voyagers. This review provides a comprehensive, 30-year perspective on this arduous journey, tracing the evolution of computational methods for modeling electrolytes and SEI from early density functional theory (DFT) calculations of isolated molecules to modern artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) frameworks that promise to accelerate materials discovery. We organize the methodological development into five generations, each representing a milestone in this ongoing voyage: static DFT (1995–2005) establishing thermodynamic foundations; ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) for interfacial dynamics (2005–2010); AIMD integrated with free energy calculations to elucidate electron transfer and rare events (2011–2015); quantitative design rules, space charge effects, and mechanical properties (2016–2020); and advanced DFT techniques combined with MLIPs, generative models, large language models, and self-driving laboratories (2021–2026). We critically assess classical MD, reactive force fields (ReaxFF, eReaxFF), hybrid HAIR methods, kinetic Monte Carlo, and Monte Carlo approaches, demonstrating how each method bridges the chasm between electronic structure and mesoscale phenomena. The review further examines ML applications—from property prediction and spectroscopic signature forecasting to MLIPs achieving first-principles accuracy at classical force-field speeds, generative molecular design, high-throughput screening, active learning, and integration with autonomous experimentation. We identify persistent challenges that continue to test the field’s resolve: long-range electrostatics, transferability across chemical space, time-scale bridging, uncertainty quantification, and data standardization. Practical recommendations for method selection are provided, accompanied by a comprehensive comparative table. This review establishes that the integration of DFT, AIMD, MD, ReaxFF, kMC, MLIPs, and AI has created a powerful multiscale modeling ecosystem, transforming battery research from trial-and-error to rational, data-driven design.

item.title: Tumour accumulation is not tumour-to-liver selectivity: a publication-aware polymer nanoparticle reanalysis
item.description: Selecting a polymer nanoparticle solely for tumour accumulation can ignore competing liver uptake. We quantify the relationship between these ranking objectives using paired whole-organ biodistribution measure-ments from the publicly archived Nano-Tumor Database. The primary cohort contains 142 source-labelled Polymeric formulations in 72 connected publication-reference groups, evaluated at 24 hours without temporal extrapolation. Analyses include publication-cluster bootstrap intervals, within-publication active/passive con-trasts, fixed baseline prediction models and prespecified time/material sensitivity analyses. Median tumour and liver accumulation were 0.625%ID and 9.750%ID. Tumour accumulation and the tumour/liver ratio had Spearman correlation 0.561 (publication-bootstrap 95% interval 0.396 to 0.707); only 47.2% of the top-quartile formulations overlapped between objectives. The equal-weight within-publication active/passive log10-ratio contrast was 0.209 (0.091 to 0.325) across 15 overlapping publication groups. Additional objective-weight, publication-omission and capacity ablations preserve the primary cohort. Leave-one-group-out within-publication contrasts range from 0.183 to 0.244 log10 units. The observational contrast remains confounded, and organ selectivity is not a validated safety or efficacy end-point.

item.title: Site-preference engineering of cobalt active-site ensembles in spinel oxides for oxygen evolution
Suppression of Singlet Fission in a DPH dimer by a polar solvent
item.description: Singlet fission (SF), a multiexciton generation process in organic molecules, offers intriguing possibilities to overcome limitations in multielectron photocatalysis. For this approach to be viable, SF chromophores must combine sufficiently high triplet energies with efficient SF in the polar environments typically required for photocatalytic reactions. Herein, we present a detailed investigation of the excited-state dynamics of a covalently linked dimer based on diphenylhexatriene (DPH), a high-energy SF chromophore, in a polar solvent, benzonitrile (PhCN). While the dimer undergoes SF in toluene, SF is strongly suppressed in PhCN, where the excited-state dynamics instead favour symmetry-breaking charge separation (SBCS). These results highlight solvent polarity as an important consideration in the design of highly symmetric SF chromophores for photocatalytic applications

item.title: AI Literacy among Undergraduate Chemistry Students from a Social Cognitive Perspective
item.description: AI literacy is increasingly important in undergraduate chemistry education, where students must evaluate generated explanations against chemical principles and evidence. However, the conditions shaping chemistry students’ engagement with AI remain insufficiently understood. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory, this qualitative study examined semi-structured interviews with 36 undergraduate chemistry students from 22 higher education institutions in China. Thematic analysis identified interrelated personal, behavioral, and environmental influences. Participants who expressed confidence in using AI also described selective reliance and deliberate efforts to retain responsibility for academic work. Expected benefits included efficiency and opportunities to ask questions with less perceived interpersonal judgment. Peers and senior students were prominent sources of practical guidance, often preceding formal instruction amid inconsistent institutional expectations. These findings suggest that AI literacy involves self-regulation, affective considerations, and informal social learning. For chemistry educators, they highlight the importance of supporting students’ judgment about AI-assisted explanations, creating space to discuss conceptual uncertainty, and making standards for evaluating chemical claims explicit within peer interactions. The study contributes a qualitative account of how undergraduate chemistry students understand and negotiate AI use within their learning environments.

item.title: In Silico Design and Structural Validation ofEpitope-Based Vaccine Candidates Against Feline Calicivirus using Immunoinformatics
item.description: This research aims to utilize bioinformatics methods to identify and analyze potential vaccine epitopes for feline calicivirus (FCV). FCV is a highly contagious pathogen causing respiratory illnesses in cats, posing significant challenges due to its genetic variability. The project involved retrieving FCV nucleotide sequences, predicting potential vaccine epitopes, and evaluating their antigenicity, toxicity, and allergenicity. The properties of the vaccine peptide sequence were also predicted and analyzed in 3D. There are 4 identified nucleotide sequences and 5 peptide sequences that show promising attributes of being non-antigenic, non-toxic, and non-allergenic. The methodology employed tools like IEDB, Vaxijen, AllerTOP, ToxinPred, ProtParam, Protein-Sol, SWISS-MODEL, MolProbity website, and PDBsum. Despite the genetic diversity of FCV, targeting conserved regions can potentially provide broad protection. However, further empirical validation through T-cell epitope prediction, secondary structure extrapolation, and molecular docking could be done to ensure vaccine efficacy against emerging FCV strains. Collaborative efforts in veterinary research are also emphasized to expedite vaccine development and implementation.

item.title: Vibronic Absorption and Circular Dichroism Spectra of Chiral PDI Aggregates in Free Space and Optical Cavities
item.description: Manipulating molecular chirality via strong light–matter coupling holds promise for asymmetric photochemistry and chiral optoelectronics, but a microscopic understanding of how cavity confinement, excitonic delocalization, and vibronic coupling intertwine is still lacking. We address this by simulating the polaritonic absorption and CD spectra of helical perylenediimide (PDI) aggregates in optical cavities, using a generalized Holstein–Tavis–Cummings (HTC) model parametrized from ab initioelectronic-structure calculations and solved with the non-Markovian stochastic Schrödinger equation (NMSSE). Unlike conventional HTC approaches, our model fully incorporates local excitations (LEs), charge-transfer excitations (CTEs), and their mutual couplings. We show that cavity photons generate chiroptical responses beyond the reach of standard exciton theory, yielding strong CD signals even when direct inter-chromophore coupling is negligible. This non-local chiral effect originates from collective coupling to a shared cavity mode, which allows a local excitation to coherently address distant monomers through the quantized field. We further demonstrate that dark polaritonic states are highly sensitive to packing: symmetry breaking via disorder or dipole misalignment lifts their degeneracy into three bright bands. Vibronic coupling, however, broadens the central band and redistributes intensity into sidebands, partially masking the splitting. Together, these findings reveal the microscopic origins of cavity-mediated polaritonic chirality and offer a roadmap for engineering dark states in chiral assemblies.

item.title: Physics-Guided Learning with Calibrated Uncertainty for Molecular Thermodynamics Beyond Observed Chemical Space
item.description: Scientific machine learning seeks to explore vast, high-dimensional design spaces, but experimental data are typically sparse and unevenly distributed, limiting generalization beyond observed systems. Molecular thermodynamic property prediction is a prime example. We develop a Physics-guided PC-SAFT neural NETwork, P-SANET, within a reliability-oriented framework integrating physical models, physics-guided target formulation, chemically informed out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation and monotonic error calibration. P-SANET learns the temperature-dependent charging free energy and maps it through PC-SAFT to molecular interaction parameters. This thermodynamically structured target improves prediction accuracy for scaffold-disjoint and structurally novel molecules. A matched-size open-data benchmark further shows that chemically informative coverage, rather than nominal dataset size, is a key determinant of OOD reliability. A monotonic calibrator combining temperature, ensemble uncertainty and embedding novelty provides quantitative error estimates. P-SANET achieves competitive vapor-pressure accuracy against published models and transfers without property-specific retraining to enthalpy of vaporization, liquid density and critical properties.

item.title: Competing Circular-Economy Uses of Oyster Shell Waste: Uncertainty-Aware Life-Cycle Allocation Between Reef Restoration and Low-Carbon Construction
item.description: Recovered oyster shell can be returned to the water as reef substrate, ground into cement-replacing powder, or landfilled, and coastal cities increasingly collect it. Which use is better has not been quantified under uncertainty. A per-tonne, multiobjective Monte Carlo model compares the three uses on living oysters and on net life-cycle carbon relative to disposal. Reef survival is a Bayesian predictive distribution built from four public Billion Oyster Project site counts, used as an external reference only, tested by leaving each site out and by an age-standardized variant. The concrete pathway uses joint draws of cement displacement, service-life ratio and carbon from a companion paper’s model, on a common functional basis with the avoided landfill emission credited once. Per tonne of shell, concrete use changes net carbon by a median -115 kg CO2e (P10–P90 -865 to 624) and is a net saving in 58% of draws, but this depends on durability: -421 kg in the favorable dam case, -120 in the neutral pavement case, +84 in the unfavorable marine case, and a net emission of 1,928 kg against a slag-blended cement. Reef use emits 114 kg and yields 24,533 living oysters (2,394–97,648) per tonne, and costs more carbon than OPC-referenced concrete in 68% of draws. Whether the reef is preferable is a valuation question with a median break-even of 8 g CO2e per living oyster; the share of draws in which sending all shell to the reef is optimal changes by at most 0.10 when any one site is left out. All results are conditional model predictions and not validated environmental benefits.

item.title: Chitosan as a Sustainable Loading-Density-Tunable Scaffold for Switching Energy- and Electron-Transfer Pathways in Porphyrin Photocatalysis
item.description: Support architectures critically govern the molecular organization and excited-state pathways of organic chromophores. Chitosan, one of the most widely studied sustainable, biomass-derived polysaccharides, has typically served as a low-loading, aggregation-suppressing host for photofunctional chromophores such as porphyrins. By contrast, high chromophore loading remains largely unexplored because it is generally assumed to cause detrimental aggregation-induced quenching. Here, this sustainable biopolymer is redefined as an active, high-density scaffold for controlling the excited-state branching of covalently attached platinum(II) meso-tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin (PtTCPP). PtTCPP was grafted onto partially acetylated chitosan over a broad loading range of 0.050–1.00 equivalents per glucosamine unit. At low loading (<0.25 eq), the chitosan scaffold preserved predominantly monomer-like PtTCPP photophysics and promoted Type II energy transfer to oxygen. Increasing the loading (≥0.25 eq) promoted J-type PtTCPP assembly, suppressed singlet-oxygen generation, and stabilized a long-lived, oxygen-sensitive triplet component associated with electron-transfer-dominant photochemistry. Cocatalyst-free photocatalytic hydrogen evolution served as a functional readout of this loading-induced pathway switching, reaching 74.1 mmol g-1 h-1 at 0.50 eq, with an apparent quantum yield of 0.4% at 405 nm. These findings establish chromophore loading density on chitosan as a practical design lever for directing excited-state branching between energy-transfer and electron-transfer pathways, repositioning a widely used sustainable biopolymer from a passive dispersion matrix to an active scaffold for aggregation-enabled photochemistry and solar-driven hydrogen production.

item.title: Geometric Reaction Path Alignment for Kinetic Feasibility Assessment
item.description: Automated reaction exploration can generate more candidate elementary steps than can be practically characterized with transition-state searches. Thermodynamic screening provides an inexpensive first filter, but endpoint energies contain no information about the path connecting reactants and products. Here, we introduce SPARTA (Steric Path Alignment for Reactive Transformation Assessment), a geometric kinetic proxy that generates reaction-biased endpoint conformers, refines them through iterative image-dependent pair potential path optimization, and evaluates electronic single-point energies along the resulting path. Across two large reaction-barrier datasets, the SPARTA barrier discriminates highand low-barrier reactions better than reaction energy. Across curated reaction classes, SPARTA reproduces experimentally established steric trends when kinetic differences are governed by accessibility to the reactive configuration, while identifying clear limitations for stereoelectronically or orbital-symmetrycontrolled transformations. Applied to glucose pyrolysis and formose reaction networks, a single SPARTA threshold retains more than 98% of reactions with reference barriers below 50 kcal mol−1. In the glucose network, adding SPARTA after thermodynamic screening reduces the number of candidate transitionstate searches from 13,436 to 4,760 while retaining all 241 reactions below 20 kcal mol−1. These results establish the geometric accessibility of the reaction path as a useful complement to thermodynamic screening for reducing the cost of automated reaction-network exploration.

item.title: DEL-Flow: AI-Driven Structural Generation and Activity Validation of MDM2-Targeting Macrocyclic Peptides
item.description: Macrocyclic peptides represent a promising modality for modulating intracellular protein–protein interactions; however, macrocyclic peptide datasets with reliable experimental activity measurements that can inform rational design remain limited. Here, we developed DEL-Flow, a pocket-conditioned generative framework for the design of MDM2-p53 inhibitors. Using an iterative DEL-selection strategy, a first-generation symmetric dimeric macrocyclic peptide DEL identified a half-scaffold associated with highly enriched library members, which was retained to construct a second-generation asymmetric focused DEL. Experimentally derived selection signals from this focused DEL were combined with computationally generated conformations and macrocyclic topologies for model training. DEL-Flow integrates these priors with MDM2 pocket and PackDock-derived pose information to generate side-chain variants while retaining the macrocyclic core. An SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching model generates all-atom coordinates, and a MASK denoising module predicts editable-region atom types, chirality, and bond connectivity. Starting from templates 126 and 319, DEL-Flow generated 20 candidates from each template, yielding 40 candidates in total. Following prioritization, 126-18 and 319-18 were synthesized off DNA and inhibited the MDM2-p53 interaction in fluorescence-polarization assays, with IC50 values of 1.95 and 6.50 μM and Ki values of 163 and 548 nM, respectively. These results support the use of DEL selection signals and pocket geometry to guide the generation of macrocyclic peptides absent from the original library that inhibit the MDM2–p53 interaction.

item.title: Scaled-Up Production of Graphene Oxide: Design, Simulation, and Analysis of a Stirred Tank Batch Reactor
item.description: Graphene oxide (GO) is an emerging product experiencing exponential growth in popularity and demand. This comprehensive research evaluates the technical and economic feasibility of implementing a large-scale GO production plant in Malaysia, based on existing pilot-scale data from the industry. The major aspect of the GO production process is the GO synthesis reaction, carried out in a jacketed, stirred tank batch reactor of approximately 500 L capacity. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) software COMSOL Multiphysics is used to simulate the dynamic behaviour of reactants within the reactor to obtain the best possible configurations and dimensions of the reactor. The results indicated that the reactor should have a height-to-diameter (H/D) ratio of 1.75, with an inner diameter of 0.71 m and a total height of 1.63 m. The entire proposed production process is simulated using SuperPro Designer software, and the results obtained are used to aid in the plant's equipment sizing calculations and economic analysis. A comprehensive economic analysis has assessed its profitability and economic viability. All calculations indicate that the plant would be a potentially profitable venture with a high return on investment (ROI) of 126.9% and a short payback period of 0.83 years.

item.title: Synthesis of Benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene Propellanes via [2 + 2] Photocycloadditions through Energy Transfer Process
item.description: Propellanes are molecules with unique three-dimensional (3D) structures and chemical properties. Owing to their strained and rigid molecular frameworks, propellanes have attracted considerable attention in various fields. Heteroacenes, such as benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene (BTBT), are widely used in materials science. However, there are few reports on the synthesis of heteroacene-derived propellanes. Therefore, the development of general synthetic strategies for constructing heteroacene-derived propellanes and the elucidation of the physical properties of these derivatives are of significant interest. Meanwhile, photocycloaddition via triplet energy transfer (EnT) process with photosensitizers has received considerable attention for the synthesis of 3D molecules from planar substrates. Herein, we report the photochemical synthesis of BTBT propellanes via triplet-sensitized [2 + 2] photocycloadditions. Photochemical reactions of benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene S,S-dioxide (BTBT-DO) with alkenes were performed in the presence of 4-CzIPN under visible light irradiation conditions, affording a variety of BTBT-DO propellanes. Several spectroscopic studies and control experiments support that this reaction proceeds via the EnT process. The BTBT-DO propellanes enable further derivatization, including Pd-catalyzed transformations. This strategy provides an opportunity to access heteroacene-derived propellanes in materials science.

item.title: Cross-Validation of Electrochemical, Spectroscopic, and Gravimetric Methods for Characterizing Self-Assembled Monolayers
item.description: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used to tune the properties of metal electrode surfaces, with applications ranging from sensing to electrocatalysis. However, the structure, coverage, and stability of SAMs often evolve under applied potential, and no single experimental technique provides a complete description of these changes. This work demonstrates the application of several surface characterization techniques, including voltammetric, spectroscopic, and gravimetric methods, on a model SAM system comprised of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a gold electrode. We evaluate and cross-validate these complementary techniques, discussing their ability to support inferences about dynamic surface behavior. These analyses provide information regarding molecular identity, relative orientation, surface accessibility, and adsorbate coverage; specific to the 4-MBN SAM we report for the first time the adsorption isotherm and kinetic parameters for adsorption. This study demonstrates a characterization framework to investigate SAM dynamics and aims to support contemporary in situ SAM studies within the electrochemistry and surface science communities.

item.title: Metastable hydrate of sodium chloride is a pentahydrate as revealed by 3D electron diffraction
item.description: ABSTRACT: Mixtures of water and NaCl, the archetypal salt, play important roles in industrial processes and natural environments on Earth and throughout the Solar System, yet their structural diversity at low temperatures remains poorly understood. Here, we determine the crystal structure of the metastable sodium chloride hydrate formed upon flash freezing using three-dimensional electron diffraction. Our analysis reveals a sodium chloride pentahydrate (NaCl∙5H2O), which consists of one-dimensional chains of hydrated sodium octahedra, with Cl− ions and water molecules located between the chains and linked by hydrogen-bonding interactions. NaCl∙5H2O introduces a new structural motif in the NaCl hydrate family and differs considerably from the thermodynamically stable and denser sodium chloride dihydrate that forms upon slow cooling. Fully dissociated ions in this metastable phase suggest that rapid freezing of saline solutions may provide a synthesis route to hydrates that retain local coordination environments resembling those of the parent solution.

item.title: Enantioselective intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates
item.description: The enantioselective synthesis of bicyclic dihydrouracil and sulfamide derivatives through an intramolecular 1,3-diamination of acrylates is described. The method relies on the cyclization of urea and bis-sulfamide substrates, bearing a remote conjugated p-nitrophenyl ester, in the presence of a chiral isothiourea catalyst and diphenyl phosphate as an acid additive, affording the corresponding bicyclic products in good yields (up to 97%) and with excellent enantioselectivities (typically 94:6-97:3, up to 99.5:0.5 er). The transformation proceeds through a tandem intramolecular aza-Michael addition/ lactamisation sequence, with the latter releasing the catalyst and closing the catalytic cycle. Covalent activation of the acrylate through the formation of an acyl ammonium intermediate, combined with non-covalent interactions that facilitate nucleophilic attack and organize the reactive species, provides a plausible basis for the high levels of stereocontrol observed. This metal- and oxidant-free approach overcomes the low electrophilicity of acrylates and shows that nitrogen nucleophiles can participate in isothiourea catalysis.

item.title: Achieving Accurate Prediction of Water Adsorption in Mildly Hydrophobic MOFs
item.description: Accurately predicting the steep, S-shaped water adsorption isotherms of mildly hydrophobic MOFs and other hydrophobic porous materials remains challenging. This difficulty stems from the delicate balance between framework–water and water–water interactions that governs cooperative pore filling. Here, we develop a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP), trained on reliable density functional theory reference data, for the prototypical mildly hydrophobic channel MOF MIP-211(Al). Combined with a Molecular Dynamics-based transition-matrix Monte Carlo (MD-TMMC) scheme, this accurate MLIP enables to predict the sorption isotherm in excellent agreement with the corresponding experimental data, capturing both the low-pressure gradual water uptake increase and the sharp adsorption step at P/P0 ≈ 0.3. This accuracy enables to elucidate the adsorption mechanism, from initial adsorption to complete pore filling: water first anchors through a characteristic OCOO···H2O···μ-OH dual hydrogenbond interaction motif; as these sites saturate, a secondary and competitive OCOO···H2O···H2O dual interaction motif emerges, driving cooperative self-assembly and triggering the adsorption step. At saturation, the confined water network approaches, but does not fully reach, bulk-water connectivity. This work demonstrates that combining a reliable MLIP-training level of theory with an appropriate MC strategy enables both quantitative prediction and mechanistic understanding of water adsorption, providing a foundation for the rational design of mildly hydrophobic MOFs of key interest for heat transformation technologies and water harvesting applications.

item.title: Lewis Base-Induced Valence Tautomerism in a Phosphorus Cation Enables the Activation of Strong Element-Fluorine Bonds
item.description: Main-group compounds show drastic differences in properties and reactivity between their n and n+2 oxidation states. While this often precludes transition-metal mimetic redox catalysis, precise control over prevalent oxidation states in a switchable compound could offer promising avenues for main-group-mediated processes. We demonstrate that hypercoordination-induced valence tautomerism unlocks high effective Lewis acidity in a phosphorus cation. By employing a redox-non-innocent, pincer-coordinated phosphenium(+III) cation, we enable low-barrier inversion at phosphorus coupled with valence tautomerism. Counterintuitively, adding a neutral Lewis base does not quench the cation's electrophilicity; instead, it triggers valence tautomerism, generating a formal phosphorus(+V) cation. This hypercoordinated species exhibits enhanced reactivity and is capable of abstracting fluoride from stable inorganic anions like [SbF6]-. Furthermore, in the presence of hydrosilanes, metal-free catalytic hydrodefluorination of fluoroalkanes is achieved.

item.title: A Machine Learning Approach to logBB Prediction Combining Molecular Docking and Quantum-Chemical Descriptors
item.description: Blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability is a major challenge in the development of drugs targeting the central nervous system (CNS). Computational prediction methods can help prioritize candidate compounds and reduce the experimental workload during early drug discovery. In this study, machine learning models were developed to predict the blood-to-brain concentration ratio expressed as its decimal logarithm (logBB). The objective was to investigate whether molecular docking scores obtained with AutoDock Vina for P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), together with quantum-chemical descriptors, could provide additional information for logBB prediction. The dataset comprised 685 compounds. A linear regression analysis identified eight factors associated with logBB: hydrogen bond donors, gas-phase electronic energy, electronic energy difference between water and hexane, number of heavy atoms, LogP, gas-phase geometry optimization time, number of aromatic rings, and fraction of sp3-hybridized carbon atoms. Notably, the electronic energy difference between water and hexane showed a stronger association with logBB than the corresponding Gibbs free energy difference, suggesting that electronic energy descriptors may provide complementary information. Higher-level quantum-chemical calculations will be required to investigate this finding further. Twenty-one machine learning models were evaluated. The selected support vector regression model using a radial basis function kernel (SVR-RBF; C = 0.869, ε = 0.135, γ = 0.165) was trained on 585 compounds and evaluated on a held-out validation set of 100 compounds, achieving an R2 of 0.605, an MAE of 0.368, and an RMSE of 0.459. Finally, the computational time analysis showed that descriptor generation was strongly dependent on molecular weight, with quantum-chemical calculations and molecular docking accounting for most of the computational cost. Overall, this work highlights the potential of combining physicochemical, molecular docking, and quantum-chemical descriptors for machine learning-based logBB prediction.

item.title: A Boomerang Catalyst Combining High Catalytic Activity and Reusability for Aqueous Transfer Hydrogenation of Ketones
item.description: We report a boomerang-type iridium catalyst that combines the high activity of homogeneous catalysis with spontaneous and quantitative catalyst recovery without external operation. The catalyst consists of a Cp*Ir complex immobilized on a cross-linked poly(acrylic acid) gel (PAA). Upon addition of formic acid (FA), Ir species are released into solution, enabling the aqueous transfer hydrogenation of a broad range of ketones under air without additional additives. In situ analyses confirmed the presence of soluble Cp*Ir reaction intermediates during the reaction. Upon complete consumption of formic acid (FA), the dissolved Ir species were spontaneously and quantitatively recaptured by the support without requiring temperature modulation or solvent exchange. The catalyst retains over 90% of its initial activity over five consecutive runs, with no detectable Ir remaining in the reaction solution after recovery. This autonomous boomerang mechanism provides a promising strategy for combining the high activity of homogeneous catalysts with the reusability of heterogeneous catalysts.

item.title: Structure Determination of Surface Sites in Heterogeneous Olefin Metathesis Catalysts from 95Mo NMR Signatures
item.description: Heterogeneous olefin metathesis catalysts composed of highly dispersed Mo sites on support carriers are used to produce key olefin building blocks for higher value-added products, e.g. the Shell Higher Olefin Process (SHOP). However, understanding the nature of Mo sites in catalysts, i.e. molybdenum oxides supported on amorphous supports like silica, MoOx/SiO2, is hampered by a low fraction of surface metal sites (low loading), the possible distribution of surface species and the lack of very sensitive characterization methods to distinguish subtle changes in the coordination environment of Mo sites on amorphous supports. Here, we show how 95Mo NMR spectroscopy enables identifying various Mo sites in olefin metathesis catalysts, pointing out the presence of isolated tetrahedral Mo-dioxo sites along with MoOx clusters, whose quantities depend on the preparation methods and Mo-loadings. Most notable is the use of NMR signatures as a structural refinement tool. Following a validation with molecular mono- and di-oxo Mo(VI) complexes characterized by single-crystal XRD measurements, we are able to determine the exact coordination environment, geometry and structural parameters of the dominant Mo sites, a highly dispersed dioxo Mo bis-grafted species in a tetrahedral environment with d(Mo=O) = 1.71 ± 0.07 Å, d(Mo-OSi) = 1.91 ± 0.15 Å, ∠(O-Mo-O) = 107 ± 7° and ∠(Mo-O-Si) = 140 ± 40°. This structure closely resembles this of the [MoO2(OSi(OtBu)3)2] molecular analogue. Additionally, this signature indicates a narrow distribution of Mo sites, highlighting the well-defined nature of these sites. Noteworthily, while well-defined, the large promotional effect observed upon co-feeding 2,3-dimethyl-1-butene further supports the role of nearby protons to initiate metathesis, rather than the sole nature of the isolated Mo sites themselves, hence the importance of promoters and the small fraction of active sites in their absence.

item.title: Uncovering Heterogeneous Energetic Trajectories in NiFe Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysis through Integrated Raman, Electrochemical and Microkinetic Analysis
item.description: Fe incorporation strongly modifies the activity of Ni-based electrocatalysts, but how heterogeneous surface states contribute to this behavior remain unclear due to improper understanding about intermediate evolution. Here, we investigate whether correlations between spatially resolved spectroscopic features and electrochemical responses can reveal distinct energetic and kinetic characteristics of NiFe electrodes. We combine in-situ Raman mapping, electrochemistry and microkinetic modeling to study three NiFe electrodes prepared under different Fe-deposition conditions. Potential-dependent spectra reveal site-to-site variations in NiOOH related vibrational features and higher-wavenumber oxygen-associated spectral signatures across individual surface sites. Correlation and regression analyses identify a compact set of Raman descriptors associated with the electrochemical response, while sitespecific predicted scores reveal distinct potential-dependent trajectory patterns. Raman-guided projection into a model-derived intermediate-energy space further enables comparison of these trajectory phenotypes within a common thermodynamic framework. Although the projected energetic distributions exhibit substantial overlap, their arrangement and model-estimated kinetic characteristics vary across different trajectory phenotypes and kinetic regimes. These findings suggest that spatially heterogeneous NiFe surface states may exhibit different kinetic responses under applied potential, instead of following a uniform catalytic evolution. More broadly, this study demonstrates the potential of integrating independent spectroscopic and electrochemical observations with microkinetic modelling to uncover energetic and kinetic heterogeneity in OER electrocatalysis.

item.title: Nanocorrugated Conducting Polymer–Based Electrochemical Transistors with Enhanced Ionic-Electronic Transduction for Ultrasensitive Biomolecular Detection
item.description: Electrolyte-gated organic transistor (EGOT) biosensors enable label-free volumetric biosensing, yet their performance in physiological environments remains constrained by polymer microstructure and inefficient ion–channel coupling. Here, we demonstrate that substrate-induced nanocorrugation reconfigures mixed ionic–electronic transport in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) channels. The corrugated SiO2/Si substrates alter the structural and electrochemical response of conformally deposited PEDOT:PSS channels. Structural and electrochemical measurements show changes in molecular ordering, crystalline orientation, local structural heterogeneity, and mixed ionic-electronic transport in the nanocorrugated films. Compared with flat counterparts, the nanocorrugated devices exhibit enhanced molecular ordering, improved ion accessibility, and stronger gate–channel coupling. The proposed platform enables ultrasensitive nucleic-acid detection and label-free sensing of stroke-related protein biomarkers in buffer, serum, and whole blood. For DNA sensing in buffer, the mean response exceeded the detection threshold at 20 aM, the regression-derived threshold concentration was ~15.4 aM, and statistically significant separation from the negative control began at 200 aM. IL-6 produces a concentration-dependent response down to the lowest tested concentration of 1 fM. Overall, nanoscale corrugation enables a route to tune ion transport, reconfigure the polymer network, and enhance volumetric transduction in conducting polymer EGOTs, thereby facilitating robust biosensing under physiologically relevant environments.

item.title: Diffusion-Model-Based Restart Selection for Adaptive Sampling of Adenylate Kinase: Structural Integrity Assessment and Comparison with Simple Baselines
item.description: Generative models are increasingly proposed for choosing where adaptive molecular dynamics should restart, but whether their proposals are physically sound starting points and whether they outperform simple rules has rarely been tested together. Using adenylate kinase, we first audited a workflow that reconstructs restart structures from a diffusion model's latent space: judged by per-domain native contacts calibrated on unbiased MD, most reconstructed structures were damaged from their first frame, and the rare states identified from them were partially unfolded LID domains. We then compared restart selection by a denoising diffusion probabilistic model with a latent-space Gaussian ablation, least-counts and two unbiased baselines, starting only from intact MD frames, with targets fixed and timestamped before any production run, equal simulation time and three replicates of every strategy and baseline. No strategy reached the primary target within the pre-specified 0.84 µs per series, so the binary comparison cannot distinguish them; adaptive restarts covered the reference distribution slightly better than the baselines, and in an exploratory closest-approach analysis the diffusion model did not come closer to the target than the simple strategies. The target differed from the data shown to the strategies only in a combination of domain states, which the diffusion model did not propose. Selecting starts by novelty in the latent space, with or without a learned model, tended to choose frames farther from the target than random picks, and the diffusion model's samples stayed close to the data. The value of a generative model lies in proposing structures beyond the data, yet that is the capability that produced the damaged restarts; confined to intact frames, its role reduces to a novelty rule on existing frames. We recommend domain-resolved integrity gates, pre-specified targets, simple baselines at equal simulation time and replicated runs for evaluating generative adaptive sampling.

item.title: Self-Evolving Laboratories Through Persistent Digital and Physical Adaptation
item.description: Turning a scientific idea into an experiment often requires researchers to build, configure and repeatedly adapt the labo- ratory around it. This work demands resources and specialized expertise that can place ambitious experiments beyond reach. Here we introduce a framework for self-evolving laboratories (SEL), connecting computation, physical experiments and AI models through persistent cycles of observation and revision. GPT Astra uses camera observations and physical feedback to adapt robotic actions, digital twins and CAD designs. These changes are retained as reusable skills and infrastructure, allowing the laboratory to develop alongside its scientific tasks. In our fume-hood SEL prototype, GPT Astra identified the need for a beaker holder and storage stand and generated successive designs for on-demand 3D printing. Four holder generations and two stand generations culminated in parts integrated into the robotic workflow with operator assistance. A photoresist campaign proposed by Raven, an agentic AI platform for materials discovery, connects this platform to materials fabrication. Exposure to a 405 nm continuous-wave laser in the two-photon polymerization setup produced circular features that survived development; optical microscopy and reduced acrylate-band absorbance in ATR–FTIR support polymerization and qualitative double-bond conversion. The scientific workflow connects experimental outcomes and retained capabilities to the resources needed to establish and extend them. By making laboratory capabilities reusable and adaptable, SEL offer a path towards broader participation in experimental science, empowering researchers to build and extend the tools their ideas require. Project website: https://ai4ssi.github.io/self-evolving-superintelligence-lab/.

item.title: How Molecular Weight Shapes the Relative Importance of Chemical and Structural Descriptors for Aqueous Solubility
item.description: Learning aqueous solubility remains a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as it directly influences oral bioavailability and the selection of viable drug candidates. While data-driven approaches have achieved considerable success, conventional supervised learning models often fail to fully exploit the complementary chemical and structural information encoded within molecular representations. Beyond accurate prediction, understanding the molecular features that drive solubility is essential for developing interpretable models and guiding molecular design. In this work, we propose an additive learning framework that jointly models chemical descriptors and graph-based molecular representations while providing quantitative insights into their individual contributions to solubility prediction. The framework is evaluated on a dataset comprising over 9,000 molecules with diverse structural, chemical, and electronic properties. Graph-theoretic descriptors derived from molecular connectivity are used to capture structural characteristics associated with aqueous solubility. Our analyses reveal that the relative importance of chemical and structural descriptors shows an interesting association with molecular weight: chemical descriptors dominate the structural ones below the median molecular weight, whereas graph-theoretic descriptors become increasingly influential for heavier molecules, reflecting the growing importance of atomic connectivity in determining solubility.

item.title: Machine learning–driven inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for selective Mg2+/Na+ separation
item.description: Desalination brine, a byproduct of seawater desalination, contains valuable resources, including magnesium. Recovering magnesium requires selectively retaining Mg2+ while allowing the dominant monovalent cation, Na+, to permeate. Nanofiltration (NF) membranes fabricated by interfacial polymerization are promising for this Mg2+/Na+ separation, but their performance depends on coupled formulation and processing variables that are inefficient to optimize through trial and error. Here, we demonstrate a workflow integrating dataset curation, forward prediction, and inverse design of thin-film composite NF membranes. A dataset of 1,253 entries, comprising literature and in-house records, was cleaned, imputed, and augmented through chemically constrained permutation of interchangeable polymer, solvent, and salt variables in the training split only. Optimized extremely randomized tree regressors predicted pure water permeability, solute rejection, and intermediate membrane properties, achieving test-set coefficients of determination above 0.79. Shapley analysis indicated that permeability was governed primarily by formulation and processing variables, whereas rejection depended mainly on solute identity and charge, as well as membrane tightness. Using Bayesian optimization with a scalarized objective, two membrane recipes with favorable Mg2+/Na+ selectivity were identified and experimentally validated. The inversely designed membranes exhibited the required Mg2+/Na+ selectivity, demonstrating the capability of this workflow to design Mg2+-selective NF membranes for resource recovery from desalination brine.

item.title: RxnScout: Deploying a Vision-Language Agent for Nickel-Catalyzed C-Glycosylation Condition Optimization
item.description: Reaction-condition optimization requires substantial experimental time and resources, making early candidate selection important when no target-specific yield data are available. Can pretrained chemical knowledge improve the use of the initial experimental budget? We evaluate RxnScout, a locally served vision-language model agent, in a wet-lab pilot to screen a previously unoptimized substrate pair in nickel-catalyzed C-glycosylation. RxnScout reads reaction-scheme images, selects candidates for testing from a chemist-curated set of commercially procurable reagents, and updates recommendations from measured yields. Sequential screening varies one condition dimension at a time, while a chemist reviews the accompanying rationales before execution. Wet-lab comparisons showed that RxnScout reached the best catalyst yield observed during the campaign (the campaign-best catalyst yield) in fewer trials than the baselines. We discuss deployment trade-offs, limitations, and errors in the generated rationales. A high-throughput experimentation (HTE) platform has been purchased, installed, and commissioned, providing the hardware foundation for the next deployment stage.

item.title: Removal of Cu(II) and a PET Glitter Microplastic Surrogate by Alginate, Alginate–Opuntia, and Chitosan-Treated Alginate–Opuntia Beads
item.description: The use of alginate-only beads, alginate–Opuntia (AO) beads, and chitosan-treated AO beads for the removal of Cu(II) and a PET glitter (a microplastic surrogate) from water has been investigated. The beads were shaken for 6 h in jars of water that had glitter, Cu(II), or both in them, and AO beads soaked in dilute acetic acid with no chitosan were used to check the acid. The Cu(II) removal increased by 13.72 percentage points with the addition of Opuntia and by a further 24.75 points with the chitosan post-treatment, and both increases were found in each of the three bead batches (p ≤ 0.0015). In the presence of 2.00 g of glitter, the chitosan-treated beads removed about 84% of the Cu(II), about the same as without glitter. About 8% of the Cu was also lost in the jars without beads. Meanwhile, the glitter removal increased by about 7 points with Opuntia but changed by less than 0.25 points with chitosan (batch-level p = 0.635 and 0.389). No significant difference was found between the separately run acid control and untreated AO beads. According to these results, the glitter capture of the beads was improved by the addition of Opuntia, and most of the improvement in Cu(II) removal was obtained with the chitosan post-treatment.

item.title: Perspective on the Feasibility of Near-Term Quantum Simulation for Industrially Relevant Catalyst Materials
item.description: Quantum simulation has been proposed as a route to treating strongly correlated electronic structure problems relevant to catalysis, but most existing studies focus on faulttolerant algorithms beyond current hardware capabilities. Here we assess the feasibility of near-term quantum simulation for catalytic materials through industrially relevant use cases. We consider zeolite clusters from classical QM/MM simulations relevant to NH3-SCR, and construct electronic active-space and embedding-based models of the catalytic active site. Using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansätze, we estimate qubit requirements and circuit depths to produce the ground-state for both full and reduced Hamiltonians. Direct simulation of the full system is intractable on near-term devices, but fragmentation and active-space approaches, combined with low-rank Local Unitary Cluster Jastrow ansatz constructions, substantially reduce resource requirements. These results indicate that, while full catalytic models remain out of reach, reduced representations of chemically relevant fragments begin to approach the capacity of near-term quantum hardware. This highlights the role of physically informed model reduction in applying quantum simulation to applied materials problems.

item.title: Direct Determination of Pyroelectric Coefficients in Molecular Crystals by X-ray Quantum Crystallography
item.description: Organic molecular crystals with piezoelectric and pyroelectric responses are emerging as soft, biocompatible materials for next-generation energy harvesting. However, quantifying crystal polarity in such materials—and its variations under mechanical or thermal stimuli—on a structural basis remains challenging. Here, we estimate pyroelectric coefficients directly from high-resolution X-ray quantum crystallography (QCr) via accurate modelling of hydrogen positions and electron densities. QCr modelling of a series of piezoelectric crystals reveals in-crystal molecular dipole moments (μ) and spontaneous polarization (PS) at variable temperatures (~100 and ~298 K) with pronounced crystal-field effects, including enhanced μ relative to isolated molecules and elevated PS. Temperature-dependent variations in PS (∆PS/∆T) predict pyroelectric behaviour, corroborated by variable-temperature voltage-output measurements in γ-glycine. The pyroelectric coefficients (p) and PS values thus estimated agree well with experimental measurements. The results demonstrate QCr as a powerful route to elucidating the molecular and electronic level origins of pyroelectric phenomena in crystalline materials, with potential extension to piezoelectric and ferroelectric properties.

item.title: Combining Chemical Protein Synthesis and Cell Delivery for Photoproximity Labeling in Living Cells
item.description: Mapping a protein’s local environment is essential for understanding its cellular roles. Proximity labeling (PL) identifies nearby proteins, while photoproximity labeling (PPL) adds temporal control through light activation. However, intracellular applications of these methods commonly rely on genetically encoded fusions that could alter protein localization or function and offer limited control over defined, site-specific post-translational modifications (PTMs). Here, we combine chemical protein synthesis with bead loading (BL) to enable live-cell PPL using fully chemically synthesized photocatalyst–protein of interest (PC–POI) conjugates. Synthesis enables site-specific PC attachment, while BL delivers conjugates directly into cells, bypassing endocytosis and preventing endosomal trapping. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate the strategy using chemically synthesized small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteins. Notably, PC selection was critical: conjugation to Eosin Y altered SUMO2 nuclear localization, whereas 5-deazaflavin (DF) preserved both nuclear localization and the ability to conjugate to cellular proteins. Using TAMRA–DF–SUMO conjugates, blue-light-triggered deazaflavin–diazirine energy-transfer (DarT) labeling captured nearby proteins for enrichment and quantitative proteomics. Comparing SUMO2 with its non-conjugatable variant SUMO2ΔG93 and its paralog SUMO1 showed that the approach resolves proximity profiles associated with conjugation competence and paralog identity. The biological relevance of the SUMO interactome was supported by established associations of selected proteins and by the finding that approximately 70% of proteins preferentially captured by SUMO2 over SUMO2ΔG93 were reported as SUMO2 substrates. This work establishes live-cell PPL without genetically encoded labeling fusions or target-protein overexpression, opening opportunities to investigate how defined, site-specific PTMs shape local protein environments.

item.title: How to Discover New Electrolyte Additives for Lithium Batteries: A Computational Roadmap
item.description: Electrolyte additives, present at a few weight percent or less, decide whether a lithium battery forms a stable solidelectrolyte interphase, survives high-voltage operation, tolerates trace water and HF, or resists fire. For three decades most additives were found by trial and error, and the few design rules that emerged, most famously “a lower LUMO than the solvent”, were known to fail almost as soon as they were formulated. Here we organize the computational literature on additive discovery, from the first quantum-chemical studies of vinylene carbonate (2002) to self-driving laboratories, chemical foundation models and LLM agents (2026), into a step-by-step roadmap: define the function the additive must perform; choose a descriptor that is actually predictive for that function; define and enumerate the chemical space; screen it with tiered quantum-chemical funnels; establish the decomposition mechanism; accelerate with machine learning; generate candidates beyond existing libraries; simulate the interphase the additive builds; and close the loop with automated experiments. For each step we summarize what has been established, what has only been correlated, and what has failed. We show that the hierarchy of redox descriptors (frontier orbitals → vertical and adiabatic electron affinities and ionization potentials → thermodynamic cycles → Li+-and anion-containing clusters → explicit-interface dynamics) is now quantitatively documented, that solvation-and product-level descriptors are emerging as the missing axes, and that the decisive bottleneck has shifted from candidate generation to reliable, fast, function-specific experimental labels. We close with a table of what each class of method can and cannot predict and with a realistic outline of a closed-loop additive-discovery framework.

item.title: Scalable Density-Based Bootstrap Embedding with Perturbative Triples for Large Molecular Systems
item.description: Extending density-based bootstrap embedding (BE) with perturbative triples to large molecules requires control of both fragment solver cost and tensor storage. We present a restricted and unrestricted BE-CCSD(T) implementation combining density-fitted embedding transformations, fragment parallelism, and streamed contractions of triples density contributions. Explicit one-and two-particle terms and the correction to the coupled-cluster multipliers are retained without assembling a molecular two-particle density matrix or storing a complete triples tensor. item.title: Reproducibility, Benchmarks, and Mechanistic Diversity: Building Trust in Computational Electrocatalysis for the AI Era
item.description: Computational electrocatalysis has contributed significantly to the design of electrocatalysts for energy conversion and storage. Yet three avoidable shortcomings constrain the reliability and reusability of computational results: incomplete reporting, oversimplification of reaction pathways and/or active sites considered, and inconsistent protocols for constructing free-energy changes (ΔG). Researchers may therefore be forced to repeat calculations simply to recover structures, verify reference conventions, or identify the source of conflicting results. This Perspective argues that reproducibility must encompass the full computational record: electronic-structure settings, surface models, atomic configurations, thermochemical and electrochemical corrections, and the explored reaction network. We examine the roles of surface structure, coverage, stability, mechanistic breadth, and descriptor choice under operating bias, and propose modular benchmarks spanning numerical verification, surface chemistry, electrified interfaces, and mechanistic validation. We also outline how journals and repositories can strengthen methodological transparency and Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) data deposition. Our aim is to stimulate discussion around a persistent reproducibility deficit that leads to inefficient use of computational resources, obstructs cumulative science, and leaves valuable data unavailable for benchmarking, data mining, and trustworthy artificial-intelligence-assisted discovery. More complete and standardized computational records would make results both more credible today and substantially more reusable tomorrow.

item.title: Modular Synthesis of N-Heterocycle-Substituted α-Amino Esters
item.description: Rapid analogue generation is central to early-stage drug discovery, creating demand for synthetic methods that combine modularity, operational simplicity, and broad substrate compatibility. N-Heterocyclesubstituted α-amino carbonyls are poorly served in this respect, their synthesis largely depending on a narrow pool of commercially available α-halogenated carbonyls. Here we report a one-pot three-component platform that addresses this gap through a formal reductive 1,2-aminoalkylation of ynoates, combining phosphine-catalysed a-funαtionalisation with a photoredox-mediated decarboxylative Giese reaction. The method accommodates azoles, lactams and imides alongside diverse carboxylic acids and ynoates, enables late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals, and is compatible with array-based library synthesis for rapid analogue generation.

item.title: A Latent Ability Model for Benchmarking Molecular Representations
item.description: The growing number of chemical foundation models calls for a standardized benchmarking method both for practitioners choosing representations and researchers identifying gaps. Previous work that ranked latent abilities of various chemical embeddings to predict ADMET properties suffered from significant shortcomings, including the use of biased datasets incongruent with real world usage and overstating statistically significant differences in model performance.
