We derive from first principles a variance inflation factor of (M+1)/3 for the Bayesian Bradley-Terry model evaluating M models on E endpoints at the exchangeable null and use numerical simulation to show variance inflation is still present in the non-exchangeable case. We propose a new method to directly model the margin of error as a function of latent ability and use it to evaluate models retrospectively on the datasets from the OpenADMET Polaris, ExpansionRx, and PXR competitions. We compare 35 embeddings and 13 end-to-end fine-tuned models across 17 ADMET endpoints. Although endpoint-to-endpoint variability means that no neural representation is expected to outperform ECFP on a hypothetical new endpoint in more than 95% of cases, our model concludes that 29 of 47 representations outperform ECFP in terms of latent ability with posterior probability above 0.95.

item.title: Pocket and ligand embeddings for 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank
item.description: This work presents a retrieval resource covering 72,199 protein–ligand complexes from the Protein Data Bank. Each complex carries a 1,280-dimensional pocket embedding, obtained by mean-pooling final-layer ESM-2 representations over binding-site residues within 8 Å of the ligand and computed per chain rather than over a concatenation of all polymer chains; a 2,048-bit RDKit Morgan fingerprint of the ligand, taken from the idealized Chemical Component Dictionary entry and therefore shared by complexes binding the same component (26,619 distinct fingerprints across the 72,199 rows); and HDF5 coordinates, per-residue heavy-atom centroids for the pocket and per-atom for the ligand, with residue and element identifiers. A residue-to-token mapping makes each pooled embedding reproducible from the released files. FAISS indices are provided over the two modalities separately, because they answer different questions: pocket-only retrieval recovers a same-UniProt complex at rank 1 for 81.2% of queries, whereas ligand-only retrieval is the stronger signal for chemotype search.

item.title: Correlation-Energy Extrapolation within Shell-Nested Virtual Spaces
item.description: We show that power-law extrapolation of the correlation energy can be carried from a sequence of orbital bases into a shell hierarchy within one molecular virtual space. In shell-nested virtual spaces (SNVS), atomic natural orbitals guide the radial and angular content of successive layers, and the correlating-orbital count beyond the valence-virtual space replaces the cardinal number in a two-point formula. The construction uses one Hartree–Fock reference in one parent basis. We calibrate and cross-validate the formula for 200 small molecular states of H and B–F at the MP2, CCSD and CCSD(T) levels, then test MP2 and CCSD transfer without refitting on 40 larger systems. In the standard ANO family, the full quadruple-zeta layer pair gives an MP2 RMS error of 0.79 mEh for the larger set, compared with 2.16 mEh for conventional extrapolation. Diffuse augmentation reduces the anion bias, and placing the excess functions in the valence-virtual space preserves the counting variable. The CCSD and reaction-energy tests show how the benefits depend on correlation level and error cancellation. Measured CCSD(T) workflow costs are comparable to those of the conventional pair. These results demonstrate the usefulness of atomic shell information for molecular extrapolation and motivate basis sets designed for the successive SNVS layers.

item.title: Closed-loop formulation–process optimization under unknown feasibility for extended-release pellets
item.description: Pharmaceutical formulation development frequently encounters formulation–process conditions that fail before a viable product is produced, leaving downstream performance unobservable and experimental feasibility unknown a priori. Here, we demonstrate a closed-loop formulation-development workflow that jointly optimizes formulation and process variables while learning experimental feasibility from physical outcomes. Using caffeine-loaded extended-release pellets produced by wet granulation and extrusion-spheronization, ANDROMEDA 1 selected formulation compositions and processing conditions within a large mixed categorical and numerical design space. Across 51 experiments performed in 13 sequential batches, 29 conditions produced pellets suitable for downstream characterization and 22 (43%) were infeasible. Failed experiments were retained as feasibility observations without assigning artificial drug release scores. Among feasible formulations, the best observed deviation from a predefined four-hour zero-order release target decreased from 1.63 to 0.17 fraction-hours. Release performance, pellet morphology and drug loading followed distinct trajectories, with an empirical trade-off between release deviation and median pellet aspect ratio. Retrospective Gaussian-process modelling showed that replacing an excipient-slot encoding with slot-independent material mass fractions increased leave-one-out cross validated R2 for release prediction from 0.39 to 0.60. Adding four derived wet-mass descriptors reduced release prediction R2 to 0.38 but yielded the highest morphology prediction R2 (0.64). Neither alternative representation improved forward-in-time release prediction. Together, these results show that unknown feasibility, competing product attributes and formulation representation can be incorporated within a single adaptive formulation-process workflow. Analyses further identify design space coverage and representation choice as important considerations for machine learning-guided pharmaceutical development.

item.title: Stretchable Wireless Sensing-Computing Biointerfaces Enabled by High-Voltage Megahertz Electrochemical Transistors
item.description: Combining stretchability with wireless operation is highly desirable for minimizing mechanical mismatch and reducing the electronic footprint and power burden at dynamic biological interfaces. Yet existing stretchable wireless patches based on passive radio frequency (RF) circuits can sense only physical stimuli that directly alter the resonant circuit, such as pressure, strain, and temperature, leaving no accessible electrical input for electrophysiological or chemical signals and little capacity for local computing function. Here, we realize an active RF circuit architecture using electrochemical transistors that enables both electrode-based sensing, particularly of electrophysiological and biochemical signals, and reservoir edge computing for data compression. This advance addresses the voltage and frequency incompatibility between electrochemical transistors and RF circuits by establishing a previously unexplored operating regime that suppresses ionic responses and, consequently, electrochemical degradation within the channel. Using this architecture, we demonstrate fully implanted cardiac electrogram recording, wound-attached chemical sensing, and wireless reservoir computing for tactile-pattern recognition. Overall, this design substantially expands the capabilities of stretchable wireless platforms to encompass nearly all major sensing modalities together with edge computing.

item.title: Decision Framework for Polymer Composite Linings in Trenchless Renewal: Integrating Materials Durability, Operational Performance, Application Quality, and Environmental Sustainability
item.description: Polymer composite linings are increasingly used in trenchless renewal technologies. These technologies are advantageous when material durability, structural requirements, application quality and service exposure are considered together, yet renewal decisions are still made largely case by case, often overlooking some of these aspects. This paper develops an evidence-based decision framework in which every decision rule is an explicit, traceable statement linked to measured or published evidence. The evidence base integrates long-term hygrothermal ageing of reinforced polyester and elastomer-modified epoxy linings, linings removed from service after up to ten years, measured application quality, cure kinetics, material identity verification and environmental assessment. Screening flowcharts decide whether to renew, repair or replace and which lining system or polymer composite is technically suitable; an evidence matrix then compares the remaining options with stated evidence levels; and a staged quality assurance and quality control protocol, linked to a defect–cause–control table, makes application quality verifiable. Three asset archetypes demonstrate how it routes decisions and what records each decision must leave.

item.title: EnGOAT: An Energy–Geometry Analysis Toolkit for Free-Energy Surfaces of Mobile Species in Crystalline Materials
item.description: The free-energy surface (FES) of a mobile species in a crystalline host governs its behavior within the material, including properties such as adsorption and transport, but reducing it to quantitative descriptors remains challenging. We present the Energy–GeOmetry Analysis Toolkit (EnGOAT), an open-source framework for the energetic, geometric, and topological analysis of volumetric FES data. Building on the TuTraSt algorithm, EnGOAT partitions the FES into basins and transition states, quantifies their volumes, surface areas, and energy–volume histograms, represents their connectivity as periodic graphs from which minimum-energy pathways and merge trees are obtained, and computes directional self-diffusion coefficients by kinetic Monte Carlo. Because accessibility is defined from energy isosurfaces of the FES rather than from van der Waals radii, the extracted descriptors are probe-specific and reflect the energy landscape actually experienced by the mobile species. Results are stored in a JSON/NumPy data model suited for high-throughput screening and can be explored with a dedicated visualization tool. We demonstrate EnGOAT for CH4 adsorption in a zeolite and for Li+ ion transport in a ceramic electrolyte.

item.title: From Boron Flatland to 3D Pharmacophore Space: Tacn-Supported Boronium Cage Cations
item.description: Replacement of C–C bonds with isoelectronic B–N units offers a compelling yet underdeveloped strategy for modulating molecular structure and electronic properties. Here we report that tacn-family ligands (1,4,7-triazacyclononane and its N-alkyl derivatives) enable the straightforward assembly of polycyclic boronium(+2) cations through a simple one-pot reaction with Me2SBHBr2 under ambient conditions. These reactions produce rigid cage structures in which three fused five-membered rings are formed in a single step via tridentate coordination of the ligand to a [BH]2+ core. The resulting boronium salts are readily isolated and exhibit remarkable thermal and aqueous stability, as demonstrated by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry. In the parent system, the N–H groups display Brønsted acidity (pKa1 ≈ 3.2) while maintaining structural integrity, with reversible protonation/deprotonation behavior observed. Electrostatic potential analyses reveal that substitution of B–N linkages for C–C bonds preserves overall molecular topology while substantially altering surface electron density, underscoring the utility of B–N/C–C isosterism for tuning intermolecular interactions. Limiting ligand donation to a bidentate mode affords a related bicyclic boronium(+1) framework containing a tertiary amine, whose geometry, reduced basicity (pKb1 ≈ 8.7), and reactivity of which are strongly influenced by the adjacent cationic boron center. Protonation yields a dication featuring a short N–H···H–B distance consistent with a dihydrogen bond, and thermal H2 elimination cleanly generates the parent tridentate boronium cage. These findings demonstrate that tacn ligands provide a general and operationally simple route to robust boronium-based cage architectures. The resulting three-dimensional, electrostatically tunable frameworks expand the accessible structural space of organoboron chemistry and suggest potential utility as scaffolds in applications where shape and charge distribution are critical, including molecular recognition and pharmacophore design.

item.title: CeO2 as a novel additive for enhancing the oxidation resistance of ZrB2–SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics: role of Ce-mediated ZrSiO4 formation
item.description: We report CeO2 as an additive for tuning oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTCs). Four compositions were compared: AlN-only, AlN-CeO2 co-doped, and two CeO2-only compositions with different SiC contents. Samples consolidated by spark plasma sintering (96-99% density) were oxidised in stagnant air at 1600 °C for up to 10 h. Ce-bearing compositions consistently outperformed the AlN-only reference. The co-doped sample showed the greatest improvement: mass gain reduced from 58 to 40 mg cm-2, oxide thickness from 1388 to 550 μm, and the SiO2-rich surface layer increased from ~5 to 82 μm. EDS-PhaSe analysis identified significant ZrSiO4 formation across Ce-containing samples. CeO2 appears to operate at two scales: enhancing borosilicate melt spreading to form a continuous surface barrier and promoting subsurface ZrSiO4 formation. CeO2, particularly combined with AlN, represents a promising strategy for improving oxidation resistance in ZrB2-SiC UHTCs.

item.title: The Liquid Structure of Ethyl Acetate and the Origin of Its Volatility
item.description: Ethyl acetate (EtOAc) is a staple solvent across the chemical industry, owing to its favourable combination of high volatility, moderate polarity, and low toxicity. These properties make it a versatile solvent capable of dissolving a broad range of organic compounds while also allowing for its rapid and efficient removal by evaporation. To obtain insights into the molecular arrangements behind EtOAc macroscopic properties, here we measure the structure of liquid EtOAc using total neutron and x-ray scattering. The first solvation shell is dominated by strong local structuring via weak C-H to carbonyloxygen hydrogen bonding which directs two adjacent EtOAc molecules into dimers. The proclivity towards forming dimers occludes the carbonyl oxygens, preventing the formation of longer-range ordering, with negligible structure in the second solvation shell underpinning its high volatility. Our work emphasises the relationship between local molecular structuring and liquids macroscopic behaviour, towards the engineering of formulations with targeted properties.

item.title: Doping-Induced Electronic Dimensional Crossover and Anisotropic Thermopower in Conducting Polymers
item.description: Thermopower is a key parameter for assessing the thermoelectric performance of conducting polymers and probing their charge transport mechanisms. Although pronounced thermopower anisotropy has been observed in aligned polymer films, its microscopic origin remains incompletely understood. Here, combining tight-binding modeling, first-principles calculations, and Boltzmann transport theory, we identify doping-induced electronic dimensional crossover as an intrinsic mechanism underlying this anisotropy. As hole doping increases, the Fermi surface evolves from closed three-dimensional pockets to configurations with quasi-two-dimensional and ultimately quasi-one-dimensional character, without requiring structural changes. These changes in Fermi-surface topology reshape the energy dependence of the directional transport distribution functions, producing pronounced thermopower anisotropy and direction-dependent sign reversals. We further show that this anisotropy can contribute substantially to the Nernst response of aligned conducting polymers. These findings establish a microscopic connection between band filling, Fermi-surface topology, and anisotropic thermoelectric transport.

item.title: TDEaseNexus: A Traceable, Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Top-Down Proteomics Data Analysis
item.description: Top-down proteomics (TDP) data analysis methods are continually evolving to extract increasingly comprehensive information from the highly complex datasets. However, researchers often need to coordinate multiple processing tools, write custom scripts, and rely on expert knowledge to fully interpret experimental results. To streamline the workflows and lower technical barriers, we present TDEaseNexus, an open-source desktop platform that unifies workflow execution, proteoform characterization, and interactive visualization through a natural-language AI agent. Through its AI-native interface and modular structure, researchers can execute adaptable TDP pipelines and perform label-free quantification, post-translational modification characterization, and positional-isomer quantification by stating their analytical goals. Domain-specific Skills and a Rust-based mass spectrometry toolkit provide deterministic calculations for modification searches, precursor-mass calibration, and spectral evidence analysis. The resulting analytical outputs can be inspected through interactive visualizations, while all analysis steps are automatically recorded for data provenance. As an open-source platform distributed with its complete analytical stack (https://github.com/Computational-TDMS/TDEaseNexus), TDEaseNexus facilitates routine TDP data interpretation and record-keeping, with the potential to broaden access to the development of new computational TDP methods.

item.title: Design, dual gelation mechanisms, and bioactive properties of fatty acid esters derived from C-1-oxidized maltose and dextrin
item.description: Sugar-fatty acid esters were synthesized by incorporating linear saturated fatty acids (C10–C22) into C-1-oxidized maltose (maltobionic acid, 4-O-α-D-glucopyranosyl-D-gluconic acid) via ester linkages. Esterification of C-1-oxidized sugars often triggers β-elimination, yielding C-2/C-3 unsaturated derivatives deoxygenated at C-3. In this study, various reaction conditions were investigated to minimize this βelimination. The resulting fully esterified product, maltobionolactone perpalmitate, gelled various oils at concentrations as low as 3 wt% and substantially enhanced collagen production in human dermal fibroblasts. Furthermore, linear saturated fatty acids were introduced into C-1-oxidized dextrin derivatives. Gelation tests revealed that controlling the degree of fatty acid substitution is critical for optimizing gelling performance. The resulting organogels exhibited superior emulsion and thermal stability compared to dextrin palmitate, a commercial organogelator.

item.title: Donor-Acceptor co-assembly of twisted 1,8-difunctionalized carbazole and naphthalenediimide
item.description: Functionalized carbazoles are versatile organic building blocks that play pivotal roles in diverse applications, particularly in charge-transfer complexes, hole-transport materials, and interfacial modifiers. In this study, we synthesized 1,8-functionalized carbazole derivatives (C1-C5) with various aryl substituents that provided extended conjugation via Mizoroki-Heck coupling reaction using our previously developed phosphine ligand-based Pd catalysis. Among them, the di(1-vinylpyrene) derivative (C4) exhibited a unique molecular conformation in which one pyrene unit is nearly coplanar with the carbazole. At the same time, the other is twisted by about 49°, resulting in a bidirectional π-stacking arrangement, as revealed by its single crystal structure. Photophysical, electrochemical, and computational studies collectively supported the influence of aryl substitution on the electronic nature of carbazole by tuning the HOMO-LUMO energy gap. AFM analysis showed that C4 self-assembled into spherical aggregates. In contrast, in the presence of naphthalenediimide (NDI8), it formed a donor-acceptor charge-transfer complex (1:2 ratio) that further self-assembled into a highly ordered, micrometer-long fibrillar structure. This long-range structural uniformity offers promising architectures for emerging applications of organic functional materials.

item.title: Tension-Limited Leaflet-Asymmetry Budding Predicts the Size and Rate of Tumour Ectosome Shedding
Thermodynamically informed and balance-preserving neural networks for direct vapor–liquid flash calculations
item.description: Pressure-temperature vapor-liquid equilibrium (PT-VLE) flash calculations are performed repeatedly in compositional-flow simulations and can dominate runtime. To reduce this cost, we propose three thermodynamically informed GibbsFlashNN models that directly predict phase state, compositions, and vapor fraction. A common allocation decoder algebraically enforces nonnegativity, composition normalization, and component-wise material balance. Training incorporates differentiable conditions derived from phase equilibrium and constrained Gibbs-free-energy minimization, supplied by a fixed equation of state or activity-coefficient model, or by a neural thermodynamic potential trained jointly with the flash network or independently pretrained and frozen. Evaluation spans eleven studies involving petroleum fluids, CO2-containing mixtures, nonideal organic and aqueous systems, and a five-component mixture. Across 3,090 held-out experimental composition values from nine systems, the proposed models achieve pooled major-component mean absolute percentage errors of 6.63–7.63%, compared with 6.62% for classical flashes using equations of state or activity-coefficient models and 8.01% for a supervised balance-preserving baseline with the same architecture. Relative to this neural baseline, the proposed models also reduce the pooled 95th-percentile absolute percentage error from 30.3% to 25.8–29.6%. Across the benchmark cases, median end-to-end inference speed-ups over the corresponding classical flashes range from 5.2 to 241.7 times, including confidence screening and reference fallback. These results support incorporating thermodynamic conditions into neural flash training to reduce aggregate prediction errors while approaching classical-flash accuracy at substantially lower inference cost.

item.title: An Expert-Augmented Deep Learning Approach for Synthesis Route Evaluation
item.description: Selecting multistep synthetic routes remains a major bottleneck in computer-aided synthesis planning because high-quality negative data are scarce and no single reported route can completely define route quality. We introduce an expert-augmented framework that combines large-scale reference-based route learning with expert-defined chemical feasibility assessment. Large-scale pre-training on literature-derived reference routes yields 60.3% top-1 reference-route recovery on held-out targets. The model’s rank-1 recommendations were feasible in 88.4% of assessed cases, comprising reported literature routes and expert-endorsed novel proposals. Expert assessment shows that disagreement with the literature reference does not necessarily imply chemical failure: 75.4% of novel rank-1 proposals were judged feasible. The pre-trained model already captures a measurable expert-feasibility signal (Spearman |ρ| = 0.46), which increases to 0.78 ± 0.05 after expert fine-tuning. On an independent multi-expert dataset, agreement with the expert majority increases from 48.0% before fine-tuning to 64.0% afterwards, compared with 64.8% agreement between a held-out expert and the majority of their peers under the same metric. Together, these results show that large-scale proxy supervision can provide scalable route prioritization, while limited expert supervision substantially improves alignment with chemical feasibility.

item.title: Catalytic Phosphorus-Based Hydrogen Atom Transfer via a Phosphinoyl Anion Relay
item.description: We report the first catalytic phosphorus-based hydrogen atom transfer system operating under redox-neutral conditions. Using an iridium photocatalyst and 10 mol% diphenylphosphine sulfide, we achieve decarboxylative reduction of diverse carboxylic acids—including peptides and pharmaceuticals—to C–H products in up to 95% yield, without stoichiometric reductants. Mechanistic studies reveal an unprecedented anionic relay: a phosphoryl radical is reduced to a phosphinoyl anion, which upon protonation regenerates the P–H catalyst. This work establishes redox-neutral catalytic turnover in phosphorus-based HAT and identifies a new elementary step in main-group radical chemistry.

item.title: Scalable Room-Temperature Synthesis of Glass-like MOF Thin Films on Arbitrary Substrates with Versatile Functionality
item.description: Metal-organic framework (MOF) glasses and glass-like materials offer unique advantages including improved flexibility, processability and mechanical stability, yet the rational, mild and scalable synthesis of uniform, large-area glassy MOF thin films remains largely unexplored and highly challenging. Herein, we pioneer the fabrication of homogeneous, ultra-smooth glass-like MOF thin films, which can be readily scaled into large-area coatings via a facile room-temperature immersion strategy. By simply placing diverse substrates into the precursor solution for 0.5 to 3 hours, continuous amorphous MOF films with nanometer-scale flatness and centimeter-to-0.3-meter scale uniformity can be readily prepared, with exceptional mechanical properties including Young’s modulus among the highest reported for typical ZIF glasses. Importantly, this unprecedented glass-like MOF film serves as a versatile guiding layer that enables the nucleation and growth of 15 different types of crystalline MOFs on various substrates, overcoming long-standing limitations of substrate dependence and lattice mismatch. This work not only establishes a facile and scalable synthetic platform for high-performance glass-like MOF thin films, but also extends its capability toward the universal growth of crystalline MOF films, unlocking promising new opportunities for device-oriented MOF thin-film materials for gas and isotope separation, electronic devices, sensing and electrocatalytic applications.

item.title: Sternstunden der Materialien: Cell membrane targeting AIEgens for bioimaging and therapy
item.description: The cell membrane is a highly dynamic biological interface that maintains cellular integrity and mediates critical physiological processes. Owing to its outermost location and involvement in disease onset and progression, the cell membrane has emerged as a prominent therapeutic target. Luminogens with aggregation-induced emission (AIE) characteristics are uniquely suited for cell membrane-targeting bioimaging and therapy. This review makes an across-the-board summary of advanced research in cell membrane-targeting AIEgens from ingenious molecular design to dazzling applications in living system. The targeting principles are systematically classified and illustrated into four main categories. Subsequently, advanced bioimaging applications are highlighted, ranging from the precise discrimination of cancer cells and spatiotemporal imaging of the nervous system to the dynamic monitoring of membrane physiological processes. Furthermore, cell membrane-targeted phototherapy in cancer treatment is discussed, emphasizing its unique ability to bypass multidrug resistance, induce immunogenic cell death, and activate systemic antitumor immunity. Finally, the current challenges and future perspectives are outlined, emphasizing precision material engineering, multimodal theranostics, and the immense potential of these AIEgens in advanced optical imaging, brain science, and clinical translation.

item.title: LinkerGen: Guided Autoregressive Generation of Organic Linkers for Reticular Chemistry
item.description: Organic linker design for reticular materials requires balancing molecular diversity with structural and chemical constraints. Here, we introduce LinkerGen, a compact SMILES-based autoregressive model guided by chemical building unit (CBU) types, numerical property targets, or text descriptions. We train and evaluate two model sizes on approximately 22 million fragment-enumerated carboxylate linkers spanning 2-linear, 2-bent, and 3-planar CBU types. Model size and sampling temperature adjust the balance between validity and novelty, while conditioning increases the yield of distinct, valid, novel candidates satisfying selected requests compared with unconditioned generation followed by filtering. Text conditioning combines molecular requirements in a single natural-language request, although its effectiveness depends on training coverage and prompt formulation. A prospective application connects literature-informed linker generation to metal–organic polyhedron (MOP) assembly and calculated binding energies for 5-fluorouracil, illustrating how chemical design hypotheses can be explored through computational screening. LinkerGen provides a steerable source of candidate building units and a basis for adaptation to other linker families and design objectives through suitable training data and conditioning information. Highlights • Generative model for reticular organic chemical building units (CBUs) widen the chemical linker space available for the design of metal-organic polyhedra. • Conditioning enriches generated populations in linkers with desired properties. • Text conditioning allows complex chemical requirements to be effectively expressed in natural language.

item.title: Effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC-AlN ultra-high temperature ceramics at 1600 °C
item.description: The effect of TaC additions on the oxidation behaviour of ZrB2-SiC based ultra-high-temperature ceramics, with and without AlN, was evaluated at 1600 °C in stagnant air. Three spark-plasma-sintered compositions were studied: ZSA721 (70ZrB2-20SiC-10AlN), ZSAT72-5-5 (70ZrB2-20SiC-5AlN-5TaC), and ZST631 (60ZrB2-30SiC-10TaC). After 10 h, ZSA721 gained 58 mg cm-2 and formed a 1388 ± 100 μm oxide layer. Partial replacement of AlN by TaC lowered the mass gain to 45 mg cm-2 and produced a thicker SiO2-rich surface layer, but the total oxide thickness remained comparable at 1357 ± 100 μm, while the SiC-depleted zone increased from 156 ± 12 to 240 ± 15 μm. To promote SiO2 formation further, we increased the SiC content (ZST631); however, oxidation of ZST631 resulted in the highest mass gain (69 mg cm-2), the thickest oxide layer (1477 ± 200 μm) and a discontinuous SiO2 scale. Our results, when contextualized with the research literature, indicate that TaC promotes cooperative degradation, potentially through porosity created by gas-evolution and restricted lateral spreading and healing of the Ta-containing borosilicate glass, thereby hindering the oxidation resistance.

item.title: Comprehensive Profiling of Microcystins in Non-Targeted LC-HR-MS Datasets using Mass Spectrometry Query Language (MassQL)
item.description: Microcystins (MC) are a critical class of toxic cyanobacterial secondary metabolites, with specific variants such as MC-LR strictly regulated in drinking water. Despite their extensive structural diversity, comprising over 300 known congeners, comprehensive environmental monitoring is severely hindered by the limited availability of commercial reference standards and public tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) spectra. To address this analytical bottleneck, we developed a non-targeted mass spectrometry-based computational workflow leveraging the Mass Spectrometry Query Language (MassQL) to enable comprehensive MC profiling. By systematically analyzing the chemical space and fragmentation patterns of all MC congeners documented in the CyanoMetDB database, we classified the congeners into nine structurally distinct groups. Subsequently, we designed and optimized a suite of MassQL queries targeting the conserved MC backbone, group-specific motifs, and individual constituent amino acids. The performance of these custom queries was rigorously evaluated following Feature-Based Molecular Networking (FBMN). Application across three independent cyanobacterial bloom datasets comprising both in-house and public data acquired via qTOF and Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry platforms demonstrated highly satisfactory analytical performance based on recall, precision, F1-scores, and Matthews Correlation Coefficients (MCC). We further demonstrated that MassQL functions as a powerful MC candidate prioritization tool orthogonal to molecular networking. By interrogating MS/MS data for specific structural motifs, this query-based approach enabled the discovery and annotation of novel MC congeners lacking public library spectra, significantly enhancing non-targeted screening for water quality and risk assessment.

item.title: Normalized Nucleic Acid Payload in Lipid Nanoparticles: A Perspective on the Harmonization of Published Data
item.description: Precise and consistent reporting of the nucleic acid payload per lipid nanoparticle (LNP) is important for advancing the understanding and development of nanomedicines. However, the reported number of RNA molecules ranges between ∼1-300 in recent investigations. To evaluate the RNA payload across investigations, we introduce and apply a normalized nucleic acid payload metric which accounts for differences in LNP size, nucleotides per RNA and N/P charge ratio. The normalized payload results in a similar value for siRNA-and mRNA-containing LNPs of different LNP sizes, where the average value of 71± 16 nucleotides/zeptoliter agrees well with the expected payload density based on molecular packing arguments. The use of normalized payload harmonizes the reported payload, complements existing payload metrics and enables comparison across samples and measurement techniques at both the single-particle and ensemble-average level.

item.title: Intermolecular Hydrogen-Bond Preorganization Enables Concerted 2e−/2H+ Transfer in the Franck–Condon Region
item.description: Concerted proton-coupled electron transfer (CPET) is central to biological and synthetic energy conversion, yet most studies focus on 1e−/1H+ reactions. The principles governing concerted multi‑proton multi‑electron transfer, as illustrated by water oxidation and CO2 reduction, remain poorly understood. Here, we use femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy to investigate a water-soluble fluoflavine. Following photoexcitation, we resolve an ultrafast branching (<120 fs) from the Franck‑Condon region. One pathway corresponds to concerted 2e−/2H+ transfer (2CPET) from water to fluoflavine and forms a long-lived reduced product; the other produces a short-lived two-electron-reduced intermediate. Kinetic isotope experiments (H2O vs. D2O) show that deuteration suppresses the 2CPET channel, shifting the population toward the two‑electron transfer pathway, further confirming the competitive branching between the two channels. pH-dependent measurements show that the 2CPET channel is progressively suppressed as the intermolecular hydrogen bonds are disrupted. DFT calculations provide a molecular-level explanation for this observation, revealing pre‑organized intermolecular hydrogen bonds in ground state with a short donor-acceptor distance (~2.0 Å) that serve as the structural basis for the ultrafast 2CPET. Our findings establish a direct spectroscopic view of 2CPET and identify hydrogen-bond preorganization as a key molecular prerequisite for efficient multi-equivalent proton-electron transfer, with H2O2 as the oxidation product, offering potential implications for photoelectrochemical energy storage.

item.title: The Limited Contribution of Structural Information Relative to Language-Model Signal in Data-Limited Cryptic Pocket Prediction
item.description: Cryptic pockets, drug-binding sites absent from a protein’s static structure but exposed through conformational change, expand the scope of druggable targets, yet remain difficult to identify computationally. PocketMiner, a structure-based graph neural network trained on molecular dynamics simulation data, predicts cryptic pocket formation from a single static structure (ROC-AUC 0.87). Recent protein language model (PLM)-based approaches report further improvements over this structure-only baseline (up to 0.93), but do so by simultaneously replacing the structural architecture with a sequence-only model and switching to substantially larger, differently-sourced training data–leaving it unclear whether these gains stem from the languagemodel signal itself or from increased training data scale. We isolate this variable directly: holding architecture family and PocketMiner’s original, small molecular-dynamics-derived training set fixed, we compare three matched variants–geometry-only (baseline), ESM2 embeddings only, and both combined (fused)–under identical training conditions. The geometry-only baseline achieves chance-level test performance (ROC-AUC 0.498), while both the ESM2-only (0.817) and fused (0.835) variants perform far above it, with statistically indistinguishable confidence intervals between the two, indicating that language-model signal alone accounts for nearly all of the achievable performance, and that structural information contributes marginally under these conditions. This result is confirmed on CryptoBench, an independent, larger benchmark (baseline 0.494 vs. fused 0.716, non-overlapping confidence intervals), and holds consistently across every pocket-formation mechanism examined in a stratified analysis. These findings suggest that a substantial share of the improvement reported by prior sequence-based methods is attributable to language-model signal itself rather than training data scale, with implications for data-efficient strategies in structure-based pocket prediction more broadly.

item.title: Critical Evaluation of Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy for State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Cells Against Battery Management System Baselines
item.description: Machine-learning models that estimate the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion cells from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) are rarely compared with models using only data a battery management system (BMS) records. Of 30 audited studies using three public datasets, one reported such a baseline. With whole cells held out, impedance brought no detectable gain over the strongest baseline on two exploratory datasets. A test on 88 independent coin cells, registered before the data were downloaded, was inconclusive (19 cells; +0.79 SOH points with impedance, 95% CI −0.07 to +1.66; smallest effect of interest 1.32). The capacity label varied strongly with cycling currents. Post hoc, with the label corrected for these currents without the test cell, impedance changed the full-life error of all 88 cells by −1.95 points (−2.86 to −1.03). With features of the previous discharge curve in the baseline, the change was −0.39 (−1.10 to +0.33). The comparison of impedance with these features, repeated as originally published, lost most of its gain within sets once the baseline received the previous discharge current, but not when models trained at 23 °C were tested at 35 °C. Impedance-based SOH studies should compare impedance with the strongest baseline a BMS can build.

item.title: Tailoring Chain-Edge C=R (R = C, O, S) Microenvironments in sp2-Carbon-Bridged 1D COFs Unlocks a ‘Moderate Balance’ Effect for Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
item.description: One-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) featuring double-chain architectures offer abundant exposed active sites for photocatalysis. However, topological constraints and entropy-driven stacking disorder severely impede their controllable synthesis, obscuring definitive structure–activity relationships. Herein, we report a series of sp2-carbon-bridged 1D COFs with atomically tailored chain-edge microenvironments (C=R-COFs, R = C, O, S) for efficient photocatalytic H2O2 production. In a water/benzyl alcohol (9:1, v/v) system under an O2 atmosphere, C=S-COF exhibited the highest H2O2 production rate of 3750.7 μmol g-1 h-1, corresponding to 1.8- and 20.0-fold enhancements over C=O-COF and C=C-COF, respectively, ranking among the best reported 1D COFs. Combined experimental and theoretical calculations reveal that the superior activity of C=S-COF stems not only from its red-shifted light harvesting (up to 810 nm), prolonged exciton lifetime, and supplementary 1O2-mediated pathway, but more critically, from an interfacial "moderate balance" effect. Specifically, endowing the chain-edge active sites with intermediate local charge density and moderate hydrophilicity reconciles competing elementary steps—simultaneously optimizing interfacial wetting, reactant (O2/H2O) activation, and H2O2 desorption, rather than maximizing a single descriptor. The “moderate balance” effect offers a new design paradigm for the development of advanced COF photocatalysts.

item.title: Adsorbate Resonance-Assisted Hydrogen Bonding across Solid Interfaces
item.description: In this work, we identify and characterize a cooperative interaction between adsorbates in which hydrogen bonding and surface-mediated bond redistribution reinforce one another across a solid interface. We show that this phenomenon, which we term adsorbate resonance-assisted hydrogen bonding (ARAHB), arises from the transfer of covalent bond character along a hydrogen-bond coordinate, coupled to bond redistribution throughout the adsorbate-surface complex. We develop a computational workflow to test and identify ARAHB among coadsorbates. Although first identified computationally, we connect ARAHB to previous experimental observations of symmetric hydrogen-bonded water/hydroxyl surface structures. Through computational screening of homo-and heteronuclear adsorbate dimers, we identify ARAHB across a range of X − H · · · Y motifs (X, Y = N, O, F). These interactions are characterized by strong adsorbate-adsorbate stabilization, substantial redistribution of surface bonding, and pronounced X − H bond elongation, demonstrating the generality of the phenomenon. We find a strong correlation between interaction energetics and geometry, culminating in nearly equalized X − H · · · Y configurations that exhibit the strongest stabilization. We find that the donor species principally determines the interaction geometry, whereas the acceptor largely governs the extent of bond redistribution. The overall stabilization reflects contributions from both species as well as the local adsorption environment. These findings establish ARAHB as a general interaction mechanism at solid interfaces and provide a framework for understanding cooperative adsorbate interactions that cannot be inferred by isolated adsorbate behavior.

item.title: Unraveling Two Nonlinear Rheological Peaks in Filled Rubber: Chain-Arm Retraction and Bound-Rubber Dynamics
item.description: Carbon-black-filled nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exhibits two maxima in its nonlinear oscillatory response, quantified here by a Fourier-based Nonlinearity Index (NLI). The higher-strain Peak I is inherited from the neat long-chain-branched matrix, whereas the lower-strain Peak II appears only after filler addition and is markedly more sensitive to carbon-black grade. We use a molecular description that separates the intrinsic dynamics of the matrix from those of the dynamically active boundrubber population. Peak I arises from the competition between backbone orientation and delayed arm retraction; matrix–adsorbed constraints shift this maximum to lower imposed strain and attenuate its amplitude without requiring a change in the underlying arm-retraction mechanism. Peak II is assigned to collective memory carried by adsorbed polymer associated with neighboring aggregate environments. Two limiting mechanisms for the loss of this interfacial memory—controlled by local shear rate or by interfacial deformation—predict distinct frequency dependences but are indistinguishable from the available single-frequency measurements. This picture connects the two nonlinear maxima to different molecular populations and suggests direct multi-frequency tests for separating matrix and interfacial contributions in filled NBR.

item.title: Multifaceted Control of Triplet-Pair Spin Dynamics in Intramolecular Singlet Fission at Room Temperature
item.description: The spin evolution dynamics of the correlated triplet pair (TT) decide the fate of the number of triplet (T1) excitons after photoexcitation in singlet fission (SF) materials, yet accurately resolving its relaxation pathways remains elusive. In this work, we systematically elucidate the spin dynamics of intramolecular SF in covalently linked TIPS-pentacene dimers with different inter-triplet exchange coupling (J) values and their dynamic fluctuations by externally perturbing the total spin Hamiltonian via the solventmediated external heavy-atom effect and the magnetic field effect. Based on transient absorption spectroscopy, we quantitatively demonstrate that the responsiveness to both perturbations is strictly governed by the J regime. While certain geometries facilitate or suppress spin mixing across spin manifolds depending on the J values, non-planar conformations eventually open an irreversible 3TT → T1 kinetic sink, channeling the initial population into a single T1 rather than two uncorrelated triplets (T1 + T1). Our findings reveal the mechanistic origins of spin-state dissipation, establishing a molecular framework for precisely steering spin evolution in exciton-multiplying architectures.

item.title: Clusteroluminescence-enabled active optical waveguiding in polyesters
item.description: Organic active waveguides are emerging as multifunctional photonic materials capable of simultaneously transmitting light and regulating optical signals through wavelength conversion and emission modulation. However, most reported systems rely on high-quality single crystals, doped matrices, or complex fabrication procedures, limiting their scalability and practical implementation. Here, we report a simple copolymerization strategy that introduces efficient clusteroluminescence into poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET)-derived copolyesters, thereby enabling active optical waveguiding in an intrinsically emissive, single-component polymer system. The excitation-dependent emission of the resulting copolyester gives rise to pronounced propagation-distance-dependent spectral evolution. During propagation, wavelength-selective attenuation and reabsorption progressively enrich the long-wavelength fluorescence component, producing emission-peak shift of up to 125 nm over 65 mm. The copolyesters are amenable to scalable synthesis and melt processing, which retain active optical waveguiding in flexible, thick, and geometrically irregular filaments. This work establishes clusteroluminescent PET-derived copolyesters as a scalable platform for active polymer photonics, with potential applications in optical encoding, visual information transmission, and flexible photonic devices.

item.title: How Chemical Evidence Shapes Mechanistic Reasoning and Prediction by Large Language Models: Fine-Grained Inference in Nucleoside-Derived Supramolecular Gelation
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) offer a distinctive capability for chemical problem solving by integrating chemical knowledge and experimental evidence through reasoning expressed in language. Yet how chemical evidence reshapes their predictions and expressed rationales is not self-evident and has received limited examination, particularly for challenging chemical problems. Here, using nucleoside-derived supramolecular gelation as a testbed, we systematically varied the evidence provided to LLMs and quantitatively evaluated their predictions and the mechanistic alignment of generated rationales. Without additional evidence, correct predictions were associated with greater alignment to literature-supported mechanisms than incorrect ones, suggesting that LLMs can draw on intrinsic chemical knowledge despite rationales remain largely general. Structurally similar gelation precedents, thought improved prediction accuracy significantly, reduced this distinction by anchoring rationales to insufficiently discriminative structural features, indicating that similarity-based evidence does not necessarily improve chemical reasoning and that prediction accuracy alone is insufficient to assess LLM performance in chemical tasks. In contrast, condition-constrained references and mechanistic information more consistently directed rationales toward chemically discriminative features, even when prediction accuracy did not improve in tandem. Together, our study highlights the importance of task-specific evidence design and quantitative rationale evaluation for reliable chemical problem solving by LLMs.

item.title: Automated Static and Dynamic Contact-Angle Analysis with Machine Learning
item.description: We present an autonomous machine-learning model, Conan-MLII, for fast, reproducible contact-angle measurement. The model was trained on >32 million synthetic images generated from Young–Laplace solutions spanning θ = 20◦–180◦, including the effects of gravity, multiple image scales and surface perturbations (roughness, reflection) as well as including sampling offsets to provide contact-point invariance. An improved contact-point identification (CPID) routine is integrated to enable autonomous processing of real images. The model produced results comparable to Young–Laplace (mean systematic underprediction ∼ 2◦) when tested on 172 experimental images drawn from multiple groups, and was much better at predicting asymmetric and low-angle cases where Young-Laplace fitting commonly misconverges. The total analysis time per image for the machine learning approach was three times faster than Young-Laplace fitting, the current best-practice approach. The model is extended to measurement of advancing and receding contact angles, showing excellent agreement with commercial tensiometers over the range 30◦ − 160◦. The model is provided as open-source for use and further development of contact angle measurement.

item.title: Fourier Transform Method for Surface Area Burial
item.description: We develop a method that uses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to efficiently calculate changes in the solvent accessible surface area (SASA) at many relative translations of two binding partners. For each binding partner, the buried surface area (BSA) is computed using the cross-correlation of a grid-based discretization of its SASA and of a solvent exclusion grid from its binding partner. This approach improves the tractability of exhaustive interface burial calculations by reducing computational complexity, making it particularly valuable for analyzing large biomolecular systems. We implemented an optimized library for Shrake-Rupley SASA by modifying sasa.cpp from MDTraj. Our approach reduces the cost of evaluating BSA at all translations within a rotation from to . One FFT pass costs 0.41–0.68 µs per translation against 0.14–1.70 s per pose for the direct calculation, a speedup of to that appears to grow with system size. Agreement with the direct calculation is close, with a root mean square error of 3.0 Å at 0.5 Å grid resolution. Possible applications of the method include virtual screening, models of biomacromolecular assemblies and aggregates, studies of protein diffusion, and thermodynamic analysis of large conformational ensembles.

item.title: Evaluating the Dimensionality of Molecular Ensembles Using Deep Neural Network Stochastic Autoencoders
item.description: Stochastic autoencoders (SAEs), which omit the Kullback–Leibler prior-matching term of variational autoencoders and are therefore suited to reconstruction rather than generative sampling, offer a nonlinear route to reducing the dimensionality of molecular ensembles, but their behavior across systems of differing size and flexibility is poorly characterized. Training SAEs on molecular dynamics trajectories of oxycodone, deca-alanine, crambin, a bromodomain–JQ1 complex, and HIV-1 protease, we find that reconstruction error plateaus at a system- and model-dependent latent dimensionality, that the effects of dropout and batch normalization are system-specific, and that SAEs yield more distinct clusters than principal component analysis (PCA) at very low dimensionality and reconstruct large data sets more accurately than the deterministic autoencoder CompressTraj at low dimensionality. With two to four latent variables, SAE reconstructions of crambin and HIV-1 protease are as accurate as PCA with 6–18 components, two latent variables span their leading principal subspace as well as 9–15 components, and a single SAE coordinate recovers the end-to-end distance of deca-alanine (R2 = 0.97, versus 0.04 for the first principal component), whereas PCA is more accurate at higher dimensionality and for the near-rigid bromodomain ensemble. Latent-space perturbations show that SAE latent variables encode nonlinear, position-dependent collective motions that vary across the learned manifold.

item.title: Supramolecular Control of Photoswitching in a Chiral Azobenzene
item.description: The photochemical behaviour of azobenzene photoswitches is strongly influenced by molecular structure and the surrounding chemical environment, while supramolecular interactions offer an additional means of modulating their switching response. We report the synthesis and photoswitching behaviour of chiral azobenzene derivatives incorporating a BINOL framework and thiourea hydrogen-bonding groups. The thiourea-containing photoswitch 1 undergoes reversible E→Z and Z→E photoisomerization while retaining its chiroptical response. Concentration-dependent NMR and DLS studies indicate self-association of 1, particularly in CDCl3, accompanied by a pronounced retardation of E→Z photoisomerization. Comparison with the thiourea-free analogue 8 suggests that, in addition to general concentration effects, thiourea-mediated interactions contribute to this behaviour. Addition of chloride leads to changes in the thiourea N–H resonances and increases the Zisomer content at the photostationary state from approximately 50% to 70%. Although the effect on the apparent E→Z half-life is modest, chloride binding also increases the thermal lifetime of the Z-isomer. These results show that thiourea-based association and guest binding influence the photochemical and thermal behaviour of the chiral azobenzene system.

item.title: Thermodynamically informed and balance-preserving neural networks for direct vapor–liquid flash calculations
item.description: Pressure-temperature vapor-liquid equilibrium (PT-VLE) flash calculations are performed repeatedly in compositional-flow simulations and can dominate runtime. To reduce this cost, we propose three thermodynamically informed GibbsFlashNN models that directly predict phase state, compositions, and vapor fraction. A common allocation decoder algebraically enforces nonnegativity, composition normalization, and component-wise material balance. Training incorporates differentiable conditions derived from phase equilibrium and constrained Gibbs-free-energy minimization, supplied by a fixed equation of state or activity-coefficient model, or by a neural thermodynamic potential trained jointly with the flash network or independently pretrained and frozen. Evaluation spans eleven studies involving petroleum fluids, CO2-containing mixtures, nonideal organic and aqueous systems, and a five-component mixture. Across 3,090 held-out experimental composition values from nine systems, the proposed models achieve pooled major-component mean absolute percentage errors of 6.63–7.63%, compared with 6.62% for classical flashes using equations of state or activity-coefficient models and 8.01% for a supervised balance-preserving baseline with the same architecture. Relative to this neural baseline, the proposed models also reduce the pooled 95th-percentile absolute percentage error from 30.3% to 25.8–29.6%. Across the benchmark cases, median end-to-end inference speed-ups over the corresponding classical flashes range from 5.2 to 241.7 times, including confidence screening and reference fallback. These results support incorporating thermodynamic conditions into neural flash training to reduce aggregate prediction errors while approaching classical-flash accuracy at substantially lower inference cost.

item.title: Ligand-Enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinated Au(III)
item.description: The formation of C–CF3 bonds is an important challenge in organofluorine chemistry. Understanding the factors governing this process is key to develop new synthetic strategies. Here, we report ligand-enabled C–CF3 coupling at tetracoordinate Au(III) centres supported by hemilabile P^N ligands. A series of well-defined Au(III) trifluoromethyl complexes bearing aryl, vinyl or alkynyl groups were prepared and shown to undergo thermal reductive elimination, affording the corresponding C–CF3 coupling products in high yields (86% on average of 17 examples). The reaction accommodates sterically hindered aryl groups and functional groups. Kinetic experiments support a first-order process, while density functional theory calculations identify a concerted reductive elimination pathway involving a three-centre transition state. The calculations further highlight the role of the hemilabile nitrogen donor, which partially dissociates during C–CF3 bond formation. The coupling also extends to a related perfluoroethyl Au(III) complex, demonstrating the potential to forge C–C2F5 bonds. Together, these findings establish P^N-chelated Au(III) complexes as a platform for studying and promoting C–CF3 bond formation, providing mechanistic insight into reductive elimination at gold and a basis for exploring new ligand-enabled transformations.

item.title: Ensemble Molecular Surface Electrostatic Potential Descriptors as Informative Features for Active Learning
item.description: Active learning ideally needs informative and inexpensive features that provide reliable uncertainty estimates. General interaction properties function (GIPF) descriptors, which encode molecular surface electrostatic potential, are informative but usually computed by density functional approximations on individual structures, which is not only costly but also neglects conformational flexibility. In this work, we compute GIPF descriptors efficiently based on force-field point charges over conformer ensembles via an automated pipeline starting from SMILES strings. We benchmark our approach against inexpensive cheminformatics descriptors on three experimental datasets, covering surfactants, peptide catalysts, and supramolecular assemblies. We evaluate prediction accuracy, screening efficiency, and uncertainty calibration. Our results demonstrate that force-field-based GIPF descriptors are complementary to cheminformatics descriptors and lead to better predictions. Additionally, we find that ensemble-based GIPF descriptors improve uncertainty calibration significantly. Accordingly, we recommend force-field-based GIPF descriptors, evaluated over inexpensive conformer ensembles, as affordable and scalable featurization method for active learning campaigns in chemistry.

item.title: Conserved recognition and divergent peripheral dynamics of designed statin analogues at human HMG-CoA reductase: ensemble docking and replicated molecular dynamics
item.description: Human 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) recognizes statins through a conserved polar binding region, while peripheral chemical differences may alter protein–ligand dynamics. We docked 13 chemically defined statin-related molecular states across six ligand-bound HMGCR crystal structures using three independent searches per state–receptor combination (234 searches). Eight selected states were then evaluated in three independently seeded 50 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations each (24 trajectories; 1.2 μs total). Protein-aligned root-mean-square displacement (RMSD) was analyzed for the entire ligand, a conserved nine-heavy-atom hydroxy-acid motif, and the complementary peripheral atoms, together with residue-level contacts. Top-ranked motif-compatible pose recovery varied between receptor structures, from 15/39 searches for 1HW8 to 38/39 for 1HWK. The G3-001 stereoisomers differed substantially in the persistence of geometric hydrogen-bond criteria involving HMGCR Glu559: median replica occupancies were 8.2% for G3-001 A (R) and 91.0% for G3-001 B (S), with higher occupancy for B in each of the three paired replica comparisons. A separate ether-chain extension (G3-005) exhibited pronounced peripheral displacement in one replica while selected recognition-site proximities remained. These computational observations identify testable relationships among receptor conformation, ligand stereochemistry, and interaction persistence.

item.title: Explainable ML force-field for evaluating protein–ligand binding energy using SO3LR
item.description: Accurate estimation of protein-ligand binding affinities remains central to structure-based drug design. Classical force fields neglect important quantum-mechanical effects, while quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods remain impractical for large biomolecular systems. Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) offer an alternative, but their performance may be inflated by training on protein-ligand complexes. Here, we introduce SO3LR-SF, a physics-based scoring framework that can be instantiated with any of the four pretrained SO3LR MLFF models, combining an equivariant message-passing network for semi-local interactions with physically motivated terms for short-range repulsion, electrostatics, and long-range dispersion. On PLA15 (15 active-site models), SO3LR-SF attains a relative interaction error of 2.1-5.8% against DLPNO-CCSD(T) references depending on the underlying SO3LR model, with SO3LR-T-M reaching 2.1%, the lowest of all tested methods. On the FEP benchmark (8 targets, 264 ligands), all SO3LR-SF variants achieve an average Spearman correlation of around 0.50, on par with the best semi-empirical quantum-mechanical method tested (0.47, GFN-FF) and with MMGBSA (0.44), and surpassing Glide (0.27). On the Wang dataset (8 targets, 199 ligands), the SO3LR-SF models reach around 0.59, matching the 0.59-0.62 range of molecular dynamics-based free-energy methods at a fraction of their cost. Each complex is scored in 3 s to 47 s on 12 CPU cores. An 8 Å trimming protocol reduces runtime threefold without loss of accuracy, and a restrained geometry optimization recovers ranking accuracy for targets with strained input structures. A multi-level explainability framework adds energy decomposition, per-atom energy contributions reported either for ligand or as 2D protein-ligand interaction maps, and 3D binding site visualization. We found that the polar SASA ratio of the binding pocket is predictive of electrostatic scoring performance, enabling estimation of ligand-ranking accuracy before scoring (r = 0.74-0.81 across models). Together, SO3LR-SF presents a fast, interpretable, and competitive scoring function for drug discovery that requires no experimental binding-affinity data for training.

item.title: Tuning supported Fe-Ag catalysts for selective acetylene hydrogenation: A combined experimental and computational study
item.description: We report the use of Fe–Ag bimetallic nanoparticles supported on α-Al₂O₃ as tunable highly active and selective catalysts for the semihydrogenation of acetylene in ethylene rich streams. The addition of silver enhances the ethylene selectivity. Experimental evidence was supported by DFT calculations predicting Gibbs free energies and adsorption energies as a function of catalyst composition. Comprehensive characterization was carried out using ICP, XRF, XRD, N₂-physisorption, TPR, STEM-EDX, and XPS. This work is inspired by the need for more sustainable catalysts beyond Pd for the removal of trace amounts of acetylene from the ethylene under front-end conditions downstream of industrial steam crackers for olefin production. Conventional Pd-based catalysts, though highly active, suffer from limited selectivity, high cost, and environmental concerns. Iron emerges as a sustainable alternative due to its abundance, low toxicity, and favorable hydrogenation activity. Incorporation of silver into iron catalysts leverages synergistic effects that allow to tune the performance of the catalysts. These effects result in enhanced catalytic activity and improved selectivity towards ethylene. The present work demonstrates a promising approach for developing cost-effective, sustainable, and highly active catalysts for industrial acetylene hydrogenation.

item.title: Surface Reconstruction Activates Bridge Sites of Rutile IrO2(110) for Oxygen Evolution Reaction
item.description: IrO2 is the state-of-the-art catalyst for oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in acid. Previous theoretical investigations are largely based on the (110) surface, with undercoordinated Ircus sites being considered as active centers under reaction conditions, whereas coordinated Irbr sites are considered spectators. Using a combination of density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics, we demonstrate that the Irbr sites reconstruct under anodic polarization leading to the formation of single-atom catalyst (SAC)-like centers. These SAC sites exhibit higher activity for OER than Ircus sites and are identified as durable under anodic polarization using a stability analysis based on a Born-Haber cycle. This work provides a framework for understanding how surface reconstruction fundamentally alters the catalytic function of known oxide surfaces by transforming spectator sites into primary active centers for energy conversion and storage.

item.title: DolphinQCT: The Light-Weighted, Python Based Quasi-Classical Trajectory Setup Tool for ORCA
Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
item.description: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing its scope to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.

item.title: Copper-Catalyzed Defluorinative Coupling of gem-Difluoroallenes with Grignard Reagents
item.description: gem-Difluoroallenes undergo copper-catalyzed defluorinative coupling with alkyl and aryl Grignard reagents to give monofluoroallenes. Using Cu(OAc)2 (10 mol%) in THF at −20 °C, eleven products are obtained in 64–95% isolated yield. The transformation replaces one fluorine atom while retaining the cumulated diene. Catalyst screening and substrate scope are described, together with a tentative carbocupration/β-fluoride-elimination pathway.

item.title: Performance and Design Limits of Membraneless Flow Electrochemical Cells: A Combined Secondary Current and Multiphase Flow Analysis
item.description: The membraneless electrolyzer concept has recently gained significant attention as an alternative electrolyzer design which is potentially more durable, flexible, and inexpensive due to the absence of any fragile membrane or diaphragm. While different conceptual designs have been put forward so far, the literature lacks clear quantitative insights on key design and performance parameters. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the membraneless design encompassing all the primary design concepts i.e. flow-by and flow-through. The study combines experimentally validated Euler-Euler coupled secondary current distribution model, Euler-Lagrange models, and an analytical mass balance model. First, the self-similarity in the parametric Euler-Euler analysis is exploited to formulate a dimensionless correlation by Buckingham Pi analysis for the average gas fraction in H2 and O2 gas plumes (99%). This correlation is complimentary to the analytical bubble mass balance equation presented here that enables simplified estimation of gas plume contours as well as maximum flow-by electrode height, inline with experimental observations. The same dimensional analysis also yields a correlation for plume contours across different operating conditions. For an operating current density of 0.2 A cm-2, Reynolds number of 1600 and 1000, and interelectrode spacing from 1 mm to 6 mm, the maximum flow-by electrode length has been estimated. It is shown with a strong enough flow i.e. Re>1000, the bulk bubble ohmic resistance can be neglected. The self-similarity of the polarization curves for the flow-through membraneless electrolyzer was also established via a Buckingham Pi dimensional analysis. Finally, the analysis draws an unbiased global comparison to assess the performance limits of membraneless electrolyzer designs quantitatively alongside the conventional alkaline electrolyzer.

item.title: Collection Effects Behind Genomic-DNA SERS Classification
Enantioselective Total Syntheses of Bousigonine A and Bisleuconothine B
item.description: Herein, we report the first enantioselective total syntheses of bousigonine A and bisleuconothine B, two heterodimeric monoterpenoid indole alkaloids. The requisite quebrachamine-type and aspidosperma-type alkaloid units were prepared divergently from a common intermediate and subsequently coupled with an eburnan-type alkaloid through bioinspired coupling reactions. The benzyl protecting group on the nitrogen played a crucial role in controlling the regioselectivity of these reactions, enabling selective bond formation at C10. Subsequent chemoselective oxidations of the coupling products furnished the characteristic quinone and N,O-acetal moieties, completing the total syntheses of both natural products. Furthermore, these synthetic studies led to a revision of the absolute configuration of bousigonine A.

item.title: Silicon‑Noded Cross-Ligation Platform Enabled by Customizable and Moisture-Stable Bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes
item.description: Connecting modules to central nodes is a powerful assembly strategy, as exemplified by DNA/RNA, MOFs, and SuFEx/PFEx chemistry. However, SuFEx and PFEx are largely confined to amine- and phenol-type modules and the alcohol modules could be problematic for SuFEx due to potential dehydroxylative reactions. Silicon‑noded cross-ligation offers an attractive alternative because both alcohols and phenols can serve as reliable modules to form stable silyl ethers, but lacks programmable stepwise ligation hubs comparable to those in SuFEx/PFEx. The most straightforward and common dichlorosilanes are not suitable for this purpose due to unpredictable over‑substitution and moisture‑sensitive intermediates. Herein, we develop moisture‑stable bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes as customizable dichlorosilane surrogates for programmable silicon‑noded cross-ligations. Systematic comparisons established a nucleofugality order for silicon-bound polyfluoroalkoxy groups (perfluoro‑tert‑butoxy >> hexafluoroisopropoxy > trifluoroethoxy) and further demonstrated that polyfluoroalkoxysilanes outperformed chlorosilanes and silyl triflates in both handling and chemoselectivity. A general synthetic platform via dephenylative silyletherification enables efficient construction of symmetrical and unsymmetrical bis(polyfluoroalkoxy)silanes with gram‑scale scalability. The resulting hubs enabled predictable, stepwise cross-ligation of diverse functionalized alcohols and phenols under mild basic conditions with broad functionalgroup compatibility. Notably, streamlined, protecting-group-free iterative assembly of the same type of dihydroxy modules, such as 4-hydroxyphenethyl alcohol, at silicon nodes was further demonstrated, guided by the DNA node–module logic and the high chemoselectivity of polyfluoroalkoxysilanes. Collectively, this work overcomes the limitations of dichlorosilane chemistry and offers a versatile platform for silicon‑noded modular assembly.

item.title: Donor-level validation of Raman spectroscopy for breast cancer subtype classification
Fe-Mediated Hydrofluorination of Piperidines: Access towards Fluorinated Iminosugars
item.description: Late-stage hydrofluorination provides access to fluorinated bioactive compounds suitable for 19F NMR monitoring of biological processes. We report Fe(III)-mediated radical hydrofluorination of highly substituted, chiral N-heterocycles containing piperidine, indolizidine and pyrrolidine scaffolds to the Markovnikov products. This method tolerated steric bulky substrates as well as substituents on nitrogen with different electronic effects. Finally, an Fe(III) catalytic system was compared with Co(II) and Ni(II) catalysts.

item.title: Oxidative Nucleophilic Aromatic ipso-Substitution for the Late-Stage Functionalization of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons with Five-Membered Rings
item.description: Nanographenes and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are promising materials for advanced organic electronics, but their late-stage functionalization remains challenging. Here, we report an ipso-substitution, in which tert-butyl groups, which are usually installed for solubility reasons, are selectively replaced by mesylates on PAHs and nanographenes bearing five-membered rings. The reaction proceeds via an oxidative nucleophilic aromatic substitution mechanism and can be implemented in oxidative cyclodehydrogenation protocols to produce substituted PAH skeletons in one pot. Density functional theory calculations (DFT) support the suggested mechanism. Post-functionalization of the mesylates is possible according to literature-known protocols and is successfully demonstrated by the introduction of ether, alkyne, and aryl substituents. By controlling the amount of oxidant and the reaction time, the method enables the synthesis of asymmetric functional hydrocarbons from symmetric precursors overcoming statistical limitations by other protocols. Selected tert-butyl groups thus act as sites for the late-stage functionalization of nanographenes and PAH dyes.

item.title: In silico cyclic-minipeptides predicting antibody-free early-diagnosis of Ebola virus
item.description: In this work, in silico cyclic-minipeptide candidates were computationally generated aiming to develop antibody-free sandwichbased early-diagnosis of ebola virus (EBOV). Presently there are few approved early-rapid EBOV diagnosis, despite many antibody-based efforts. Cyclic-minipeptides were chosen here because i) their vast sequence numbers facilitate designs fitting the diagnostic sensibility and specificity requirements, ii) they are easy and cheaper to scale-up for production, and iii) their rigidity could be more resistant to denaturing-buffers for EBOV early disinfection during assay. In this work, the earlier most abundant biomarker for EBOV infections soluble glycoprotein sGP were computationally targeted. Hundreds of ~ 100-1000-fold 9- and 12-mer candidates predicting higher affinities than previously reported antibodies were proposed here combining Boltzgen/ Prodigy with our newly developed evolutionary-mutations. By targeting complementary sGP cavities with cyclic-minipeptide candidates, possible sandwich-pairs would still require experimentally-guided explorations. Additional computational screening work may also be possible to select the best candidates for possible pan-EBOV diagnosis.

item.title: FROST II: certified Hartree–Fock limits of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon
item.description: We extend FROST (Fock radial orbital shooting with Taylor series) from atoms whose occupied orbitals are all s orbitals to closed-shell atoms with p and d shells, and report rigorous upper bounds on the Hartree–Fock (HF) energies of the closed-shell atoms from neon to xenon. Their leading digits are correct to 504 significant figures for neon, 103 for magnesium, 105 for argon and 103–106 for the heavier atoms, against previous records of 30 and 25. Three changes to the method make this possible. First, exchange with multipoles k ≥ 1 gives every canonical orbital the exponential tail of the outermost one, so all orbitals must share one wall; this also makes them exactly orthogonal. Second, over that common wall the inner shells are extremely stiff: the growing mode of the krypton 1s orbital rises by 10^1701. The equations are therefore solved by multiple shooting, with Taylor-series segments short enough that no mode grows by more than 10g, coupled by continuity conditions and solved by Newton’s method with a sparse LU factorization, so that the working precision grows with the target accuracy rather than with the stiffness. Third, a homotopy in the electron–electron coupling, from hydrogenic orbitals, supplies a starting point that converges to the ground state. The exact-rational certificate carries over to any angular momentum. Writing each radial function as P = rl+1f with f piecewise polynomial, the triangle rule k ≤ la + lb cancels the factor r−k−1 of every multipole, so all overlap, one-electron and Slater integrals are exact rationals. All 25 published digits of the quadruple-precision energies of Cinal are reproduced, as are his positions of the exchange-induced nodes of inner orbitals, which we locate to about 100 significant figures.

item.title: Dynamic vacancy redistribution shifts Pd nanoparticle coalescence from orientation-gated to defect-enabled on reduced CeO2(110)
item.description: Sintering deactivates supported catalysts, yet how mobile support defects couple to crystallographic transport anisotropy during nanoparticle coalescence remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a ternary Ce–O–Pd machine-learning interatomic potential (Ce–O–Pd MLIP) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large atomic model and validate it against density functional theory (DFT) calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD). Large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics (DPMD) simulations resolve early-stage coarsening of Pd62/Pd287 nanoparticle pairs on CeO2–x(110) and reveal direction-selective coalescence: [11̅0]-aligned pairs exhibit higher probabilities and shorter onset times than [001]-aligned pairs.
